nodes.theorem_title: The budgeted run of a polynomial-time verifier's sampler returns its question pair
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time verifier (`PolyVerifier`): a closed sampler program, a closed decider program and a polynomial $P \in \mathbb{N}[X]$, with $B(z) = P(|z|)$ for an input string $z$. The sampler is run on the encoding of the pair $(z, r)$ for a seed $r$. The budgeted sample `sampleC sd T z r` runs the program encoded by the datum `sd` on `encode (z, r)` under the cost budget $T$ with the computable evaluator `Machine.runForD`, decodes the result as a pair of bit strings, and returns $([], [])$ if the run does not finish within the budget or its result is not a pair of strings. The question pair `V.questions z r` is the sampler's output when it halts on `encode (z, r)` with a pair of strings of length at most $B(z)$, and the pair of empty strings otherwise; its components are elements of `Answers (V.B z)`, the strings of length at most $B(z)$.

Assume `V.Efficient z`: on every seed of length $B(z)$ the sampler halts within cost $P(|z| + |r|)$ with a pair of strings of length at most $B(z)$, the decider halts within cost $P(|z| + |x| + |y| + |a| + |b|)$ on every input $(z, x, y, a, b)$, and the decider rejects whenever one of $x, y, a, b$ is longer than $B(z)$. Assume also that $r$ is a seed of length exactly $B(z)$. Then

$$\mathrm{sampleC}\ (\mathrm{encode}\ V.\mathrm{sampler})\ \big(P(|z| + B(z))\big)\ z\ r \;=\; \big((V.\mathrm{questions}\ z\ r)_1,\ (V.\mathrm{questions}\ z\ r)_2\big),$$

the right-hand side being the pair of underlying bit strings of the two answers.

This is the identification of the computable table of the game $G_z$ with its question distribution: the tabulation `tabOf` builds the question weights of the table from `sampleC` at exactly this budget, and the lemma is what `mu_clause`, hence `quantumValue_tab` and the inclusion of the paper's class in the computable one (`MIPStar.toComputable`), rest on.

**Formalization Note** `sampleC` is total: `Machine.runForD` iterates the machine's step function $3T$ times and returns `none` when the configuration reached is not final, and both that case and a decoding failure give the junk value `([], [])`. The budget is written `V.bound.eval (z.length + V.B z)`, which is $P(|z| + |r|)$ with $|r| = B(z)$. `V.questions` has the fallback `(emptyAnswer, emptyAnswer)`; the statement says that under the hypotheses it is not taken. The arguments `z` and `r` are implicit, `V` is a section variable, and the proposition is `MIPRE.PolyVerifier.sampleC_eq`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 12 lines. It reduces to two imported theorems: `MIPRE.Cost.Eval.deterministic`, the determinism of the timed semantics in result and cost, and `MIPRE.Cost.Machine.runs_of_runForD`, the soundness of the budgeted evaluator. Three helper lemmas from the source modules are pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: The tabulated game's distribution is the doubled distribution of $G_z$
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time verifier and $z$ an input with `V.Efficient z` (sampler and decider halt within the polynomial budgets, and the decider rejects overlong strings). The game $G_z$ (`V.game z`) has questions and answers in `Answers (V.B z)`, the strings of length at most $B(z) = P(|z|)$; its distribution is $\mu_z(x, y) = \#\{r : |r| = B(z),\ \mathrm{questions}(z, r) = (x, y)\} / 2^{B(z)}$ and its predicate is acceptance by the decider. Its doubled game `(V.game z).doubled` is the synchronous game on $\mathrm{Bool} \times \mathrm{Answers}(B(z))$ whose distribution at $(p, q)$ is $\mu_z(p_2, q_2)$ when $p_1 = \mathrm{false}$ and $q_1 = \mathrm{true}$, and $0$ otherwise.

The table `V.tab z` is a `GameData` computed from the encoded sampler, the encoded decider and $P$: with $N$ the number of strings of length at most $B(z)$, its question alphabet is $\mathrm{Fin}(2N)$ and its answer alphabet $\mathrm{Fin}(N)$ (as `Fin (nX + 1)`, `Fin (nA + 1)` with $nX = 2N - 1$, $nA = N - 1$); its weight list puts one unit of weight, for each seed $r$ of length $B(z)$, at the index pair $(\mathrm{qIdx}(\mathrm{false}, x_r), \mathrm{qIdx}(\mathrm{true}, y_r))$, where $(x_r, y_r)$ is the budgeted sample `sampleC` on $r$ and $\mathrm{qIdx}(t, x) = \mathrm{idxOf}(x) + N\cdot[t]$. `(V.tab z).game` is the table read as a game, with distribution the normalized weight. `V.eX z : Fin (nX + 1) ≃ Bool × Answers (B z)` is the index equivalence sending $i$ to the tagged string at index $i$. Then for all $i, j$ in `Fin ((V.tab z).nX + 1)`,

$$(V.\mathrm{tab}\ z).\mathrm{game}.\mu\ i\ j \;=\; (V.\mathrm{game}\ z).\mathrm{doubled}.\mu\ (e_X\, i)\ (e_X\, j).$$

Together with `D_clause` this is the hypothesis of `quantumValue_eq_of_equiv` behind `quantumValue_tab`: the table has the quantum value of $G_z$, which is what makes a polynomial-time verifier a computable map from strings to explicit games.

**Formalization Note** `(V.tab z).game` is `GameData.game`, i.e. `g.syncGame.toGame`, whose distribution is `if g.totalWeight = 0 then (if x = 0 ∧ y = 0 then 1 else 0) else questionWeight x y / totalWeight` with natural-number weights cast to $\mathbb{R}$; the fallback point mass is part of the definition, and the statement asserts the equality of the two real numbers for every index pair. `V.eX z` is `finCongr (tab_nX z)` followed by `qEquiv (V.B z)`. The hypothesis `h : V.Efficient z` is required, `z` is implicit and `V` is a section variable.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 53 lines. It reduces to three imported theorems: `MIPRE.PolyVerifier.sampleC_eq` (the budgeted sample is the question pair on an efficient input), `MIPRE.Verifier.sum_filter_length` and `MIPRE.Verifier.answerEquiv_symm_val` (counting and indexing lemmas on the answer alphabet). Twelve helper lemmas from the source modules are pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: Reading back the tabulated acceptance list of a polynomial-time verifier
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time verifier, $z$ an input with `V.Efficient z`, and let $i, j$ range over `Fin ((V.tab z).nX + 1)` and $k, l$ over `Fin ((V.tab z).nA + 1)`, the question and answer indices of the table `V.tab z`. The acceptance list `(V.tab z).acc` is a list of quadruples of natural numbers: for each quadruple $(x, y, a, b)$ of strings of length at most $B(z) = P(|z|)$ on which the budgeted decider run returns `true` — `Machine.runForD` on `encode (z, x, y, a, b)` under the budget $P(|z| + |x| + |y| + |a| + |b|)$ returns `some (encode true)` — it contains $(\mathrm{qIdx}(\mathrm{false}, x), \mathrm{qIdx}(\mathrm{true}, y), \mathrm{idxOf}(a), \mathrm{idxOf}(b))$, where $\mathrm{qIdx}(t, x) = \mathrm{idxOf}(x) + N\cdot[t]$ and $N$ is the number of strings of length at most $B(z)$. `V.eX z` is the equivalence from question indices to tagged strings `Bool × Answers (B z)` and `V.eA z` the one from answer indices to `Answers (B z)`. `V.Accepts z x y a b` means that the decider halts on `encode (z, x, y, a, b)` with output `encode true`. Then

$$\big((i, j, k, l) \in (V.\mathrm{tab}\ z).\mathrm{acc}\big) \iff \Big((e_X\, i)_1 = \mathrm{false}\ \wedge\ (e_X\, j)_1 = \mathrm{true}\ \wedge\ V.\mathrm{Accepts}\ z\ (e_X\, i)_2\ (e_X\, j)_2\ (e_A\, k)\ (e_A\, l)\Big),$$

where the indices are cast to natural numbers on the left and the tagged questions and answers are read as their underlying bit strings on the right.

This is the acceptance half of the correspondence between the table and the doubled game $G_z$; `D_clause` is its restatement at the level of the decision predicates, and `quantumValue_tab` follows.

**Formalization Note** Membership is list membership of the tuple `((i : ℕ), (j : ℕ), (k : ℕ), (l : ℕ))` in `(V.tab z).acc`, which is `accListLE (V.B z) (qIdx (V.B z) false) (qIdx (V.B z) true) (accC (encode V.decider) V.bound z)`. The projections `.1`, `.2.1` and `.1` extract the tag, the string of a tagged question and the string of an answer. The equivalences `eX`, `eA` are noncomputable. The hypothesis `h : V.Efficient z` is required; `z` is implicit and `V` a section variable.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 20 lines. It reduces to three imported theorems: `MIPRE.Cost.Eval.deterministic` (determinism of the timed semantics), `MIPRE.Cost.Machine.runs_of_runForD` (soundness of the budgeted evaluator) and `MIPRE.Verifier.answerEquiv_symm_val` (the indexing of the answer alphabet). Ten helper lemmas from the source modules are pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: The tabulated game's decision predicate is the doubled predicate of $G_z$
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $V$ be a polynomial-time verifier, $z$ an input with `V.Efficient z`, $i, j$ question indices in `Fin ((V.tab z).nX + 1)` and $k, l$ answer indices in `Fin ((V.tab z).nA + 1)`. The table `V.tab z` read as a game, `(V.tab z).game`, has the decision predicate of a game description: `D i j k l` is `false` when $i = j$ and $k \neq l$ (unequal answers to equal questions always lose), and otherwise `decide ((i, j, k, l) ∈ acc)`, membership of the index quadruple in the acceptance list. The doubled game `(V.game z).doubled` of $G_z$ has the predicate `D p q a b = if p.1 = false ∧ q.1 = true then G.D p.2 q.2 a b else false`, where the predicate of $G_z$ is `G.D x y a b = decide (V.Accepts z x y a b)`, acceptance by the decider of the strings underlying $x, y, a, b$. With `V.eX z`, `V.eA z` the index equivalences of the table,

$$(V.\mathrm{tab}\ z).\mathrm{game}.D\ i\ j\ k\ l \;=\; (V.\mathrm{game}\ z).\mathrm{doubled}.D\ (e_X\, i)\ (e_X\, j)\ (e_A\, k)\ (e_A\, l),$$

an equality of Booleans.

With `mu_clause` this is the second hypothesis of `quantumValue_eq_of_equiv` that gives `quantumValue_tab`, the equality of the quantum values of the table and of $G_z$ on an efficient input.

**Formalization Note** Both sides are `Bool`. The left side includes the game description's veto `if i = j ∧ k ≠ l then false`, the right side the tag test of the doubled game; the statement asserts their equality at every index quadruple, including the diagonal $i = j$. The hypothesis `h : V.Efficient z` is required, `z` is implicit, `V` is a section variable, and the proposition is `MIPRE.PolyVerifier.D_clause`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 15 lines. It reduces to one imported theorem, `MIPRE.PolyVerifier.acc_mem_iff`, which reads the acceptance list of the table back as acceptance by the decider on the doubled question set. One helper lemma from the source modules is pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: Soundness of the budgeted evaluator: whatever it returns is a genuine run
nodes.natural_language_statement:
The ambient cost model has programs `Prog` (de Bruijn variables, `nil`, constants, `cons`, `elim`, `let_` and `loop`) acting on binary trees `Data`, with a timed big-step semantics `Eval env p r t`: in the environment `env`, $p$ halts with result $r$ at cost $t$. `p.Runs x r t` is `Eval [x] p r t`, the run of $p$ on the single input $x$. `Machine.runForD pd x k` is the computable budgeted evaluator: from the datum `pd` encoding a program and the input $x$, it iterates the machine's step function $3k$ times from the initial configuration and returns `some` of the result if the configuration reached is final, and `none` otherwise. Let $p$ be a program, $x$ and $r$ data and $k$ a natural number, and assume `runForD (encode p) x k = some r`. Then

$$\exists\, t \in \mathbb{N},\qquad p.\mathrm{Runs}\ x\ r\ t .$$

This is one of the two directions of the correctness of the budgeted evaluator; with its converse `runForD_eq_some` (a run of cost at most $k$ is found) it gives `runForD_eq_some_iff`, the decision procedure that lets the tabulations of verifier games fill in their acceptance tables by budgeted runs.

**Formalization Note** No bound on the cost $t$ is asserted; the conclusion is existential in the cost. `encode p` is `Prog.toData p`, the program as data. The budget $3k$ and the step function are internal to `runForD`; the hypothesis is an equation between values of type `Option Data`. The arguments `p`, `x`, `r`, `k` are implicit and the proposition is `MIPRE.Cost.Machine.runs_of_runForD`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 11 lines. It reduces to one imported theorem, `MIPRE.Cost.Machine.halts_iff`, which relates a terminating run of the machine to a derivation of the timed semantics. No helper lemmas are pasted: the upload consists of the imported theorem and the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: The polynomial-time halting reduction halts on the empty input exactly when the semidecider halts
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $S$ be a program of the ambient model that is closed with one input (`S.WellScoped 1`: every variable is bound in a one-entry environment) and $z$ a bit string. `Halts p x` means $\exists\, r\, t,\ \mathrm{Eval}\ [x]\ p\ r\ t$: $p$ halts on the input $x$. `haltingReduction S : PolyTimeFun BitStr Prog` is the polynomial-time function $z \mapsto \mathrm{hardcode}\ (\mathrm{onLeft}\ S)\ (\mathrm{encode}\ z)$: `hardcode p d` is the s-m-n transformation, the program running $p$ on the pair `cons d input`, and `onLeft p` is the program that on an input `cons d v` runs $p$ on $d$ (and on `nil` halts with `nil`). Then

$$\mathrm{Halts}\ (\mathrm{haltingReduction}\ S\ z)\ \mathrm{nil} \iff \mathrm{Halts}\ S\ (\mathrm{encode}\ z).$$

With `exists_semidecider`, which turns an r.e. predicate on strings into such an $S$ halting exactly on its members, this gives `exists_polyTime_reduction`: every r.e. predicate on strings many-one reduces, in polynomial time, to halting on the empty input. This is the reduction the polynomial-time halting instance of the MIP* = RE argument consumes.

**Formalization Note** `haltingReduction S z` is definitionally `hardcode (Prog.onLeft S) (encode z)` (`haltingReduction_apply`); the `PolyTimeFun` structure carrying the program and its time bound is coerced to its function. `encode z` for a bit string is the list encoding `Data.ofList Data.ofBool z`, and `.nil` is the empty datum. The hypothesis `hS : S.WellScoped 1` is required and `S` is implicit; no running-time bound appears in the statement, which is about halting only.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 19 lines. It reduces to two imported theorems, `MIPRE.Cost.hardcode_time` and `MIPRE.Cost.hardcode_time_rev`, the forward and backward transfer of runs through the s-m-n transformation `hardcode`. One helper lemma from the source modules is pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: Playing a tensor-product strategy on the restriction of a game to the support of its questions keeps the value
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $X, Y, A, B, X', Y'$ be finite types. A game $G$ on $(X, Y, A, B)$ consists of a probability distribution $\mu$ on $X \times Y$ and a decision predicate $D : X \to Y \to A \to B \to \mathrm{Bool}$. Let $G'$ be a game on $(X', Y', A, B)$ with the same answer alphabets, and $e_X : X' \hookrightarrow X$, $e_Y : Y' \hookrightarrow Y$ embeddings such that (i) $G'.\mu\ x'\ y' = G.\mu\ (e_X x')\ (e_Y y')$ for all $x', y'$; (ii) whenever $G.\mu\ x\ y \neq 0$, $x$ is in the image of $e_X$ and $y$ in the image of $e_Y$; (iii) $G'.D\ x'\ y'\ a\ b = G.D\ (e_X x')\ (e_Y y')\ a\ b$ for all $x', y', a, b$. A tensor-product strategy $S$ for $G$ consists of dimensions $d_A, d_B$, a unit vector $\psi \in \mathbb{C}^{d_A} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{d_B}$ and projective measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ on $\mathbb{C}^{d_A}$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ on $\mathbb{C}^{d_B}$; its value is $\sum_{x, y, a, b} \mu(x, y)\,[D(x, y, a, b)]\, \mathrm{Re}\,\langle \psi, (A^x_a \otimes B^y_b)\psi\rangle$. The relabeled strategy `S.relabel G' eX eY (Equiv.refl A) (Equiv.refl B)` is the strategy for $G'$ with the same state and the measurements $A^{e_X x'}_a$ and $B^{e_Y y'}_b$. Then

$$\big(S.\mathrm{relabel}\ G'\ e_X\ e_Y\ \mathrm{id}_A\ \mathrm{id}_B\big).\mathrm{value} \;=\; S.\mathrm{value} .$$

This is one half of `quantumValue_restrictQuestions`: a game whose question distribution is supported on the image of two embeddings has the quantum value of its restriction. Its consumer is the class verifier of the polynomial-time halting reduction, whose game has every string of length at most $B$ as a question while its sampler only produces strings of one fixed length.

**Formalization Note** `relabel` accepts arbitrary maps on the questions and equivalences on the answers; here the answer equivalences are `Equiv.refl A` and `Equiv.refl B`. Hypothesis (ii) is `∀ x y, G.μ x y ≠ 0 → (∃ x', eX x' = x) ∧ (∃ y', eY y' = y)`. The value is the real part of a complex inner product computed with the Kronecker product `⊗ₖ` of matrices. No `Nonempty` instances are assumed, in contrast with `value_relabel_invFun`. `X'`, `Y'`, `G` are implicit; `S`, `G'`, `eX`, `eY` explicit.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 27 lines and self-contained: it imports no theorem of the development and pastes no helper lemma from the source modules, so the upload is the statement and its proof alone.

nodes.theorem_title: Playing a strategy of the restricted game on the whole game through retractions of the embeddings keeps the value
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $X, Y, A, B, X', Y'$ be finite types with $X'$ and $Y'$ nonempty. Let $G$ be a game on $(X, Y, A, B)$ (a distribution $\mu$ on $X \times Y$ and a Boolean decision predicate $D$) and $G'$ a game on $(X', Y', A, B)$, and let $e_X : X' \hookrightarrow X$, $e_Y : Y' \hookrightarrow Y$ be embeddings with (i) $G'.\mu\ x'\ y' = G.\mu\ (e_X x')\ (e_Y y')$ for all $x', y'$; (ii) whenever $G.\mu\ x\ y \neq 0$, $x$ is in the image of $e_X$ and $y$ in the image of $e_Y$; (iii) $G'.D\ x'\ y'\ a\ b = G.D\ (e_X x')\ (e_Y y')\ a\ b$ for all $x', y', a, b$. Let $S'$ be a tensor-product strategy for $G'$: dimensions $d_A, d_B$, a unit vector $\psi \in \mathbb{C}^{d_A} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{d_B}$ and projective measurements $\{A^{x'}_a\}$, $\{B^{y'}_b\}$, with value $\sum_{x', y', a, b} \mu'(x', y')\,[D'(x', y', a, b)]\,\mathrm{Re}\,\langle \psi, (A^{x'}_a \otimes B^{y'}_b)\psi\rangle$. Write $r_X = $ `Function.invFun eX` and $r_Y = $ `Function.invFun eY` for retractions of the embeddings (left inverses, chosen with the axiom of choice). The relabeled strategy `S'.relabel G (invFun eX) (invFun eY) (Equiv.refl A) (Equiv.refl B)` is the strategy for $G$ with the same state and the measurements $A^{r_X x}_a$, $B^{r_Y y}_b$. Then

$$\big(S'.\mathrm{relabel}\ G\ r_X\ r_Y\ \mathrm{id}_A\ \mathrm{id}_B\big).\mathrm{value} \;=\; S'.\mathrm{value} .$$

This is the other half of `quantumValue_restrictQuestions`: with `value_relabel_of_support` it shows that a game whose question distribution is supported on the image of two embeddings has the quantum value of its restriction to $X' \times Y'$.

**Formalization Note** `Function.invFun` needs `Nonempty X'` and `Nonempty Y'`, which is why these instance arguments appear; it is noncomputable and takes an arbitrary value off the image. The answer equivalences are `Equiv.refl`. Hypothesis (ii) is `∀ x y, G.μ x y ≠ 0 → (∃ x', eX x' = x) ∧ (∃ y', eY y' = y)`. The value uses the Kronecker product `⊗ₖ` and takes the real part of the inner product. `X'`, `Y'`, `G'` are implicit; `S'`, `G`, `eX`, `eY` are explicit.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 28 lines and self-contained: it imports no theorem of the development and pastes no helper lemma from the source modules, so the upload is the statement and its proof alone.

nodes.theorem_title: The value of the constant synchronous strategy is the acceptance mass of its fixed answer pair
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $X$ and $A$ be finite types, with decidable equality on $A$, and $G$ a synchronous game on $(X, A)$: a probability distribution $\mu$ on $X \times X$ and a decision predicate $D : X \to X \to A \to A \to \mathrm{Bool}$ with $D(x, x, a, b) = \mathrm{false}$ whenever $a \neq b$. A synchronous strategy for $G$ is a dimension $d > 0$ together with a question-indexed projective measurement $\{M^x_a\}$ on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$ (self-adjoint idempotents summing to the identity for each $x$); its value is $\sum_{x, y, a, b} \mu(x, y)\,[D(x, y, a, b)]\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}(M^x_a M^y_b)/d$. For $a_0 \in A$, the constant strategy `const G a₀` has $d = 1$ and $M^x_a = 1$ if $a = a_0$ and $0$ otherwise, for every question $x$. Then

$$(\mathrm{const}\ G\ a_0).\mathrm{value} \;=\; \sum_{x \in X}\ \sum_{y \in X} \mu(x, y)\cdot [D(x, y, a_0, a_0)],$$

where $[\cdot]$ is $1$ for `true` and $0$ for `false`.

Together with `isPCC_const` (the constant strategy is PCC) this gives `Verifier.hasPerfectPCC_of_accepts_diagonal`: a decider that accepts a fixed answer on every question pair has a value-$1$ PCC strategy, the trivial strategy behind the "yes" instance of the halting reduction's classes.

**Formalization Note** `SyncStrategy.value` is `tracialValue G (normalizedTrace (Fin d)) P`, the generic tracial value against the dimension-normalized trace, and `value_eq` writes it out as the sum above. The right-hand side is a finite real sum of `G.μ x y * (if G.D x y a₀ a₀ then 1 else 0)`. The game `G` is an explicit argument here (elsewhere in the file it is a section variable), and the proposition is `MIPRE.SyncStrategy.value_const`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 18 lines and self-contained: it imports no theorem of the development and pastes no helper lemma from the source modules, so the upload is the statement and its proof alone.

nodes.theorem_title: The tracial value of a projective measurement family in a synchronous game is at most one
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $X$ and $A$ be finite types with decidable equality on $A$, and let $\mathcal{A}$ be a ring with a star structure and a $\mathbb{C}$-module structure (`Ring 𝒜`, `StarRing 𝒜`, `Module ℂ 𝒜`; no norm is assumed). Let $G$ be a synchronous game on $(X, A)$: a probability distribution $\mu$ on $X \times X$ and a decision predicate $D : X \to X \to A \to A \to \mathrm{Bool}$ rejecting unequal answers to equal questions. A tracial state $\tau$ on $\mathcal{A}$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear functional with $0 \le \tau(m^* m)$ for all $m$ (in the partial order of $\mathbb{C}$), $\tau(1) = 1$ and $\tau(mn) = \tau(nm)$. A projective measurement family $P$ on $(X, A)$ in $\mathcal{A}$ is a family of operators $M^x_a \in \mathcal{A}$ with $(M^x_a)^* = M^x_a$, $M^x_a M^x_a = M^x_a$ and $\sum_a M^x_a = 1$ for every $x$. The tracial value is
$\mathrm{tracialValue}\ G\ \tau\ P = \sum_{x, y, a, b} \mu(x, y)\,[D(x, y, a, b)]\,\mathrm{Re}\,\tau(M^x_a M^y_b)$. Then

$$\mathrm{tracialValue}\ G\ \tau\ P \;\le\; 1 .$$

The synchronous value (the instantiation at $\mathcal{A} = \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ with the normalized trace) and the commuting-operator value are both instances of the tracial value, so this one inequality gives `SyncStrategy.value_le_one`, `syncValue_le_one` and the bounded-above-ness that the suprema defining the values require.

**Formalization Note** The generality is a star ring with a complex module structure, not a C*-algebra. The definition takes the real part of $\tau(M^x_a M^y_b)$ so that it carries no proof obligation. `G`, `τ` and `P` are explicit arguments; `X`, `A`, `𝒜` and their instances are section variables, and the proposition is `MIPRE.tracialValue_le_one`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 26 lines. It imports no theorem of the development; two helper lemmas from the source modules are pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: The carry loop of the binary increment program runs within an explicit cost bound
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Binary numerals are bit strings written least significant bit first, and `inc` is their successor: $[] \mapsto [\mathrm{true}]$, $\mathrm{false} :: l \mapsto \mathrm{true} :: l$, $\mathrm{true} :: l \mapsto \mathrm{false} :: \mathrm{inc}\ l$. The increment program works in two phases; the first is the loop of the body `incBody` on a state `cons (encode rest) (encode acc)`: at the end of `rest` or at a `false` bit it stops with the pair `(true :: acc, rest')`, and at a `true` bit it moves a `false` onto `acc` and continues. The function this phase computes is `incAcc : BitStr → BitStr → BitStr × BitStr`, with `incAcc [] acc = (true :: acc, [])`, `incAcc (false :: r) acc = (true :: acc, r)` and `incAcc (true :: r) acc = incAcc r (false :: acc)`.

Let $l$ and $acc$ be bit strings, `env` an environment (a list of data), and $S$ a natural number with $|\mathrm{encode}\ l| + |\mathrm{encode}\ acc| + 3\,|l| \le S$, where $|\cdot|$ on data is `Data.size`, the number of nodes. Then

$$\exists\, t \le (|l| + 1)(S + 21),\qquad \mathrm{Eval}\ \big(\mathrm{cons}\ (\mathrm{encode}\ l)\ (\mathrm{encode}\ acc) :: env\big)\ (\mathrm{loop}\ \mathrm{incBody})\ \Big(\mathrm{cons}\ \big(\mathrm{encode}\ (\mathrm{incAcc}\ l\ acc)_1\big)\ \big(\mathrm{encode}\ (\mathrm{incAcc}\ l\ acc)_2\big)\Big)\ t .$$

This is the main lemma behind `incProg_runs`, the cost bound of the increment program; the increment is what enumerates the bit queries $0, 1, 2, \dots$ in the compressor's decider of the halting reduction.

**Formalization Note** `Eval env p r t` is the timed big-step semantics of the ambient model; `.loop b` iterates `b` on the state held in variable $0$, where `b` returns `cons flag s'` and a `nil` flag stops the loop with result `s'`. The state is the head of the environment and `env` is an arbitrary tail. `encode` on bit strings is the list encoding `Data.ofList Data.ofBool`, so $|\mathrm{encode}\ l| \le 4|l| + 1$. The bound is stated in terms of the parameter $S$, any number above the given combination of sizes, rather than directly in $l$ and $acc$. All of `l`, `acc`, `env`, `S` are explicit; the proposition is `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.incLoop_runs`.

nodes.theorem_title: The increment program computes the successor of a binary numeral within an explicit cost bound
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $l$ be a bit string, read as a binary numeral least significant bit first, and let `inc l` be its successor ($[] \mapsto [\mathrm{true}]$, $\mathrm{false} :: l \mapsto \mathrm{true} :: l$, $\mathrm{true} :: l \mapsto \mathrm{false} :: \mathrm{inc}\ l$). The increment program is `incProg = let_ (cons (var 0) nil) (let_ (loop incBody) revOntoProg)`: it pairs the input with an empty accumulator, runs the carry loop `incBody` (which moves the carried bits onto the accumulator and stops at the first `false` bit or at the end), and reverses the accumulator back onto the rest with `revOntoProg`. `p.Runs x r t` means `Eval [x] p r t`: the program $p$ on the input $x$ halts with result $r$ at cost $t$, in the timed big-step semantics of the ambient model. Then

$$\exists\, t \le (|l| + 2)\,\big(8\,|\mathrm{encode}\ l| + 8\,|l| + 60\big),\qquad \mathrm{incProg}.\mathrm{Runs}\ (\mathrm{encode}\ l)\ (\mathrm{encode}\ (\mathrm{inc}\ l))\ t ,$$

where $|\mathrm{encode}\ l|$ is the size (node count) of the encoded string.

`incProg_runs_nat` specializes this to canonical numerals `n.bits`, where `inc n.bits = (n + 1).bits`; that is the form in which the compressor's reading loop steps from the bit query $i$ to $i + 1$.

**Formalization Note** `encode l` is the list encoding `Data.ofList Data.ofBool l`, of size at most $4|l| + 1$ (`esize_bitStr_le`), so the bound is quadratic in $|l|$. `inc` is defined on all bit strings and the statement assumes no canonicity (no condition on the last bit). `incProg` is closed (`incProg_wellScoped`). The argument `l` is explicit and the proposition is `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.incProg_runs`.

It reduces to two imported theorems: `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.incLoop_runs`, the run and cost of the carry loop, and `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.revOntoProg_runs`, the run and cost of reversing one list onto another. Two helper lemmas from the source modules are pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: A verifier with polynomially bounded programs and sampler dimension is $\lambda$-bounded for some $\lambda$
nodes.natural_language_statement:
A normal form verifier $V$ with $\ell$ levels (`Verifier ℓ`) consists of a sampler — a closed program `sampler.prog` with a dimension function $s = $ `sampler.dim` $: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and conditionally linear data — and a decider, a closed program, such that the decider accepts only questions of the sampler's dimension. `PolyBounded f` means $\exists P \in \mathbb{N}[X],\ \forall n,\ f(n) \le P(n)$. `Prog.HasPolyCost p` means that there are a polynomially bounded $C : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a degree $k$ such that for every index $n$ and every datum $d$, $p$ halts on `cons (encode n) d` within cost $C(n)\,(|d| + 1)^k$. `V.IsBounded λ` (blueprint `def:lambda-bounded`) says: for every $n \ge 2$, $s(n) \le n^\lambda$, the sampler halts on every input `cons (encode n) d` within cost $n^\lambda (|d| + 1)^\lambda$, and so does the decider (`TimeBoundAt n (n ^ λ) λ`); and the description length $|V| = \max(|\mathcal{S}|, |\mathcal{D}|)$ is at most $\lambda$. Assume `PolyBounded V.sampler.dim`, `V.sampler.prog.HasPolyCost` and `V.decider.prog.HasPolyCost`. Then

$$\exists\, \lambda \in \mathbb{N},\qquad V.\mathrm{IsBounded}\ \lambda .$$

`IsBounded` is the hypothesis every class membership of the halting reduction carries, and until this result nothing inhabited it unconditionally. Its threshold form `exists_isBounded` ($\exists n_0, \forall n \ge n_0, V.\mathrm{IsBounded}\ n$), which the classes consume, follows by monotonicity in $\lambda$; `Halting/WrapperCost.lean` discharges the `HasPolyCost` hypotheses for the verifier a string denotes.

**Formalization Note** The time clauses of `IsBounded` are guarded by $2 \le n$; `TimeBoundAt n T k` is `∀ d, HaltsWithin prog (cons (encode n) d) (T * (d.size + 1) ^ k)`, with `encode n` the binary encoding of $n$ and `d.size` the node count of the datum. The size clause `V.size ≤ lam` is part of `IsBounded` and is met by the $\lambda$ asserted. The verifier `V` is an explicit argument and `ℓ` implicit; the proposition is `MIPRE.Verifier.exists_isBounded_lam`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 13 lines. It imports no theorem of the development; three helper lemmas from the source modules are pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: A decider that accepts one fixed answer on every question pair has a value-one PCC strategy
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $V$ be a normal form verifier with $\ell$ levels, $n$ an index and $T$ an answer-length bound. The question alphabet `V.Questions n` is $\mathbb{F}_2^{s(n)}$ with $s = $ `V.sampler.dim`, and `CL.toBits x` is the bit string of coordinates of a question $x$. `Answers T` is the type of bit strings of length at most $T$. `V.decider.Accepts n x y a b` means that the decider halts on the encoding of $(n, x, y, a, b)$ with output `encode true`. The game `V.game n T` has questions `V.Questions n` distributed as the sampler prescribes, answers in `Answers T`, and accepts $(a, b)$ at $(x, y)$ exactly when `Accepts n (toBits x) (toBits y) a.1 b.1`. Its doubled game `V.doubledGame n T` is the synchronous game on $\mathrm{Bool} \times$ `V.Questions n` in which Alice's questions carry the tag `false`, Bob's the tag `true`, and every other tagged pair has probability zero and is rejected. `V.HasPerfectPCC n T` says that some synchronous strategy $S$ of the doubled game is PCC — its projective measurements commute at every question pair of nonzero probability (`S.IsPCC`) — and has `S.value = 1`.

Let $a_0 \in$ `Answers T`, and assume that for all $x, y \in$ `V.Questions n`,
`V.decider.Accepts n (CL.toBits x) (CL.toBits y) a₀.1 a₀.1`. Then

$$V.\mathrm{HasPerfectPCC}\ n\ T .$$

This is the paper's "trivial strategy: for all questions the players return a fixed answer", and it is where the yes-instance $y_{\mathrm{yes}}$ of the classes of the compressibility criterion comes from.

**Formalization Note** No synchronicity (`IsSynchronousAt`) is asked of the decider: `HasPerfectPCC` is defined on the doubled game `(V.game n T).doubled`, whose distribution gives equal tagged questions probability zero. The hypothesis quantifies over all question pairs of `V.Questions n`, including pairs of probability zero, and `a₀.1` is the underlying bit string of the answer. `n`, `T` are implicit, `a₀` explicit, `V` a section variable, and the proposition is `MIPRE.Verifier.hasPerfectPCC_of_accepts_diagonal`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 13 lines. It reduces to one imported theorem, `MIPRE.SyncStrategy.value_const`, the value of the constant synchronous strategy as the acceptance mass of its fixed answer pair. One helper lemma from the source modules is pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: One iteration of the compressor's reading loop on a bit answer
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let `univ` be a closed program (`univ.WellScoped 1`), the universal machine the compressor's decider queries, run on inputs `cons (encode c) v`. The reading loop of the decider has the state `cons cD (cons iD acc)`: a description datum `cD`, the current bit index `iD` in binary, and the bits read so far `acc`, most recent first. Its body `readBody univ` takes the state apart, runs `univ` on `cons cD iD`, and on the answer `encode false` (`nil`) or `encode true` (`cons nil nil`) increments the index with `incProg` and pushes the bit onto the accumulator, returning the new state under the continue flag `cons nil nil`; on any other answer it stops. Let `cD`, `iD`, `acc` be data, $i$ a natural number with `iD = encode i` (the binary encoding, least significant bit first), $b$ a Boolean and $t$ a cost, and assume `univ.Runs (cons cD iD) (encode b) t`: the universal machine on `cons cD iD` halts with the bit $b$ at cost $t$. Then

$$\exists\, t' \le t + 3|c_D| + 4|i_D| + |acc| + 2\,(\mathrm{size}\ i + 2)\big(8\,\mathrm{esize}\ i + 8\,\mathrm{size}\ i + 60\big) + 30,\qquad \mathrm{Eval}\ [\mathrm{cons}\ c_D\ (\mathrm{cons}\ i_D\ acc)]\ (\mathrm{readBody}\ \mathrm{univ})\ \Big(\mathrm{cons}\ (\mathrm{cons}\ \mathrm{nil}\ \mathrm{nil})\ \big(\mathrm{cons}\ c_D\ (\mathrm{cons}\ (\mathrm{encode}\ (i + 1))\ (\mathrm{cons}\ (\mathrm{encode}\ b)\ acc))\big)\Big)\ t' ,$$

where $|\cdot|$ is `Data.size`, $\mathrm{size}\ i$ is `Nat.size i` (the binary length of $i$) and $\mathrm{esize}\ i$ is the size of `encode i`.

This is the step case of `readLoop_runs`: one bit of the described string is read and the index advanced, at a cost explicit in the sizes of the state and the cost of the query, so that the accounting of the compressor's decider can be done from these lemmas alone.

**Formalization Note** `Eval env p r t` is the timed big-step semantics; the body runs in the one-entry environment holding the state. The result `cons (cons nil nil) s'` is the loop's "continue with state `s'`" signal. `encode (i + 1)` is the binary encoding of $i + 1$ and `encode b` is `Data.ofBool b`. `cD` is an explicit section variable, `univ` an implicit one; `iD`, `acc`, `i`, `t` are implicit and `hU`, `hi`, `b`, `h` explicit. The proposition is `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.readBody_bit`.

nodes.theorem_title: The compressor's reading loop reads the described string from a succinct description
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $U$ be an efficient universal machine (`UniversalMachine`): a closed program `U.univ` with an overhead polynomial `U.bound`, such that a run of a program $c$ on $v$ with result $r$ at cost $t$ gives a run of `U.univ` on `cons (encode c) v` with result $r$ within cost `U.bound.eval (esize c + v.size + t)`, and `U.univ` halts on `cons (encode c) v` only if $c$ halts on $v$ with the same result. `IsSuccinctDesc c n x` says that $(c, n)$ succinctly describes the bit string $x$: $c$ is closed, $|x| \le 2^n$, and for every $m$, $c$ on `encode m` halts with `bitQueryAnswer x m` within cost $(n + 1)(\mathrm{size}\ m + 1)^2$, where `bitQueryAnswer x m` is `encode` of the $m$-th bit of $x$ for $m < |x|$ and the marker `ofNat 2` otherwise. The reading loop iterates `readBody U.univ` — one bit query through the universal machine per iteration — on the state `readState cD x i = cons cD (cons (encode i) (encode (x.take i).reverse))`. `readIter U s n L` is the explicit per-iteration cost for a description of size $s$ at parameter $n$ and a string of length at most $L$: the overhead polynomial evaluated at $s + (4\,\mathrm{size}\ L + 1) + (n + 1)(\mathrm{size}\ L + 1)^2$, plus the bookkeeping terms $3s + 4(4\,\mathrm{size}\ L + 1) + (4L + 1) + 2(\mathrm{size}\ L + 2)(8(4\,\mathrm{size}\ L + 1) + 8\,\mathrm{size}\ L + 60) + 30$. Let `env` be any environment. Then

$$\exists\, t \le (|x| + 1)\big(\mathrm{readIter}\ U\ (\mathrm{esize}\ c)\ n\ |x| + 1\big),\qquad \mathrm{Eval}\ \big(\mathrm{readState}\ (\mathrm{encode}\ c)\ x\ 0 :: env\big)\ \big(\mathrm{loop}\ (\mathrm{readBody}\ U.\mathrm{univ})\big)\ \big(\mathrm{encode}\ (\mathrm{reverse}\ x)\big)\ t .$$

This is the loop of `readProg`, the first stage of the compressor's decider: the string to be compressed is recovered from its succinct description by bit queries instead of being hardcoded as in the paper's machine 𝓕.

**Formalization Note** The initial state `readState (encode c) x 0` is `cons (encode c) (cons nil nil)`, since `encode 0` and `encode []` are both `nil`; the result is the encoding of the reversed string, which `readProg` reverses afterwards. `readIter` is noncomputable only through the evaluation of `U.bound`; `size` is `Nat.size` and `esize c = (encode c).size`. `c`, `n`, `x` are implicit, determined by `hsd`; `U` and `env` are explicit. The proposition is `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.readLoop_runs`.

nodes.theorem_title: The reading program recovers the string from a succinct description, within an explicit cost bound
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $U$ be an efficient universal machine (a closed program `U.univ` with an overhead polynomial `U.bound` and the two simulation guarantees `time_le` and `halts_of`), and let $(c, n)$ succinctly describe the bit string $x$ (`IsSuccinctDesc c n x`: $c$ is closed, $|x| \le 2^n$, and $c$ answers every bit query $m$, given in binary, with `bitQueryAnswer x m` within cost $(n + 1)(\mathrm{size}\ m + 1)^2$). The reading program is `readProg univ = let_ (cons (var 0) (cons nil nil)) (let_ (loop (readBody univ)) revProg)`: from the input `encode c` it builds the initial state (index $0$, nothing read), runs the reading loop, whose body queries one bit through `univ` and advances the index, and reverses the accumulated bits with `revProg`. `p.Runs x r t` is `Eval [x] p r t`, and `readIter U s n L` is the explicit per-iteration cost of the loop for a description of size $s$ at parameter $n$ and a string of length at most $L$. Then

$$\exists\, t \le (|x| + 1)\big(\mathrm{readIter}\ U\ (\mathrm{esize}\ c)\ n\ |x| + 1\big) + (|x| + 2)(4|x| + 14) + \mathrm{esize}\ c + 7,\qquad (\mathrm{readProg}\ U.\mathrm{univ}).\mathrm{Runs}\ (\mathrm{encode}\ c)\ (\mathrm{encode}\ x)\ t .$$

This is the first stage of `prepProg`, the compressor's decider of the halting reduction: it reads the string it has to compress from the description $c$, where the paper's machine 𝓕 hardcodes its own description. The run and its cost feed `prepProg_runs` and the accounting of the decider (blueprint `lem:halt-construction`).

**Formalization Note** `esize c = (encode c).size` is the size of the program $c$ as data, and `encode x` is the list encoding of the bit string. The bound is a closed-form expression in $|x|$, $n$ and `esize c`, noncomputable only through the polynomial `U.bound` inside `readIter`. The arguments `c`, `n`, `x` are implicit, determined by the hypothesis `hsd`; `U` is explicit, and the proposition is `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.readProg_runs`.

nodes.theorem_title: The two frozen programs of a described verifier fit under the size bound of the compressor's accounting
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $G$ be a gap-preserving compression (`GapCompression`: a compressed sampler family `G.sampler : ℕ → CL.Sampler 7`, a polynomial-time `G.samplerProg : PolyTimeFun ℕ Prog` computing its program from the parameter, the compression map `G.compress : PolyTimeFun ((Prog × Prog) × ℕ) Prog`, the bounds, and the completeness and soundness guarantees), and $U$ an efficient universal machine. For a bit string $x$, `Vof G U x : Verifier 7` is the verifier $x$ denotes: the compressed sampler at the parameter `descLam x` the string denotes and the decider datum `descDecD x` it denotes, wrapped in the question-length check (`Verifier.ofSamplerDeciderD`). `frozen G U x n = (Vof G U x).freeze (2n + 1)` is that verifier frozen at index $2n + 1$: its sampler and decider programs are `freezeProg (2n + 1)` of the originals, which on an input `cons N d` run the original on `cons (encode (2n + 1)) d`. `esize p = (encode p).size` is the size of a program as data. The bound is $\mathrm{fBound}\ G\ U\ L\ n = \mathrm{sampBound}\ G\ L + \mathrm{kBound}\ n + 53 + (\mathrm{wBound}\ G\ U\ L + \mathrm{kBound}\ n + 53)$, with $\mathrm{sampBound}\ G\ L$ the evaluation of the time-bound polynomial of `G.samplerProg` at $L + 1$, $\mathrm{kBound}\ n = 4\,\mathrm{size}\ n + 5$ (with $\mathrm{size}\ n$ the binary length `Nat.size n`), and $\mathrm{wBound}\ G\ U\ L = \mathrm{sampBound}\ G\ L + (L + 1) + 2\,\mathrm{esize}\ U.\mathrm{univ} + \mathrm{wrapNodes}$, where `wrapNodes` is the constant node count of the wrapped decider's description. Then for every bit string $x$ and every $n$,

$$\mathrm{esize}\ (\mathrm{frozen}\ G\ U\ x\ n).\mathrm{sampler.prog} + \mathrm{esize}\ (\mathrm{frozen}\ G\ U\ x\ n).\mathrm{decider.prog} \;\le\; \mathrm{fBound}\ G\ U\ |x|\ n .$$

The pair of frozen programs is the input handed to `G.compress` in the last stage of the compressor's preparation `prepProg`; this bound on its size is what `prepBound` passes through `G.compress.timeBound`, and `prepProg_runs` and the cost accounting of the decider use it.

**Formalization Note** The bound depends on $x$ only through its length `x.length`, and no hypothesis is made on $x$: every string denotes a verifier, well formed or not. `fBound` is noncomputable only through the evaluation of the polynomial `G.samplerProg.timeBound`. `G` and `U` are section variables and `x`, `n` explicit arguments; the proposition is `MIPRE.Halting.esize_frozen_le`.

nodes.theorem_title: The compressor's preparation computes the compressed decider's description from a succinct description
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $G$ be a gap-preserving compression (`GapCompression`, providing the compressed samplers, their program `G.samplerProg` and the compression map `G.compress`) and $U$ an efficient universal machine. `prepProg G U` is the closed program that, on `encode (c, n, λ)` $=$ `cons (encode c) (cons (encode n) (encode λ))`, does everything the compressor's decider does before its last step: it reads the string $x$ that $c$ describes with `readProg U.univ`, parses $x$ into the parameter `descLam x` and the decider datum `descDecD x` the string denotes, computes the encoded compressed sampler program at that parameter, builds the encoded wrapped decider, freezes both programs at index $2n + 1$, and runs `G.compress.code` on the pair of frozen programs and $\lambda$. The expected output is `compressedD G U x n λ = encode (G.compress (((frozen G U x n).sampler.prog, (frozen G U x n).decider.prog), λ))`, where `frozen G U x n = (Vof G U x).freeze (2n + 1)` is the verifier $x$ denotes, frozen at $2n + 1$. `prepBound G U s n L l` is the explicit sum of the stages' cost bounds, in the description size $s$, the level $n$, a bound $L$ on the string's length and the size $l$ of the parameter. Assume `IsSuccinctDesc c n x` ($c$ is closed, $|x| \le 2^n$, and $c$ answers every bit query about $x$ within cost $(n + 1)(\mathrm{size}\ m + 1)^2$), and let $\lambda$ be any natural number. Then

$$\exists\, t \le \mathrm{prepBound}\ G\ U\ (\mathrm{esize}\ c)\ n\ |x|\ (\mathrm{esize}\ \lambda),\qquad (\mathrm{prepProg}\ G\ U).\mathrm{Runs}\ \big(\mathrm{encode}\ (c, n, \lambda)\big)\ \big(\mathrm{compressedD}\ G\ U\ x\ n\ \lambda\big)\ t .$$

This is the forward run of all but the last stage of the compressor's decider `haltProg` (obligation O4 of blueprint `rem:compression-abstract`, program half); `haltProg_runs`, `haltProg_runs_inv` and the acceptance agreement `haltProg_accepts_iff` rest on it.

**Formalization Note** The decider is the paper's machine 𝓕 with the recursion removed: the string to compress is read from $c$ rather than hardcoded, the verifier compressed is `Vof G U x` frozen at $2n + 1$, and the paper's step of running 𝓜 for $n$ steps is absent. `prepBound` is noncomputable only through polynomial evaluation and contains the term `G.compress.timeBound.eval (fBound G U L n + l + 2)`. `c`, `x`, `n` are implicit and determined by `hsd`, `lam` is explicit, `G` and `U` are section variables; the proposition is `MIPRE.Halting.prepProg_runs`.
nodes.source: https://github.com/vidick/MIPRE-formalization/blob/70cbf1c52e3d5e1dff1162fdf952c9a9f4bd99ed/MIPRE/Foundations/Halting/Compressor.lean#L634-L742; blueprint lem:halt-construction; paper recursive.tex, fig:halt_f (the compressor's decider is the paper's machine 𝓕 with the recursion removed)

Twenty helper lemmas from the source modules are pasted into the upload alongside the main proof.

nodes.theorem_title: Inversion for the compressor's decider: it halts only if the universal machine halts on the compressed decider
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $G$ be a gap-preserving compression and $U$ an efficient universal machine (a closed program `U.univ` with its overhead polynomial and simulation guarantees). The compressor's decider before hardcoding, `haltProg G U`, is the closed program that on an input `cons P d` — with $P$ = `encode (c, n, λ)` and $d$ the decider's own input — runs the preparation `prepProg G U` on $P$ to obtain the description of the compressed decider, pairs that description with $d$, and runs `U.univ` on the pair, returning its result. `compressedD G U x n λ` is the encoding of `G.compress` applied to the sampler and decider programs of the verifier $x$ denotes, frozen at index $2n + 1$, and to $\lambda$. `p.Runs x r t` is `Eval [x] p r t`. Assume `IsSuccinctDesc c n x` ($c$ is closed, $|x| \le 2^n$, and $c$ answers every bit query about $x$ within cost $(n + 1)(\mathrm{size}\ m + 1)^2$), let $\lambda$ be a natural number, $d$ and $r$ data and $t$ a cost, and assume `(haltProg G U).Runs (cons (encode (c, n, λ)) d) r t`. Then

$$\exists\, t',\qquad U.\mathrm{univ}.\mathrm{Runs}\ \big(\mathrm{cons}\ (\mathrm{compressedD}\ G\ U\ x\ n\ \lambda)\ d\big)\ r\ t' .$$

With the forward run `haltProg_runs` this gives `haltProg_accepts_iff`: the decider with $(c, n, \lambda)$ in front accepts exactly what the compressed decider of the frozen verifier of $x$ accepts; from it `comprStr_accepts`, the field `CompressorSpec.accepts_compr` of obligation O4 of blueprint `rem:compression-abstract`, follows (blueprint `lem:halt-construction`).

**Formalization Note** No cost bound is asserted on $t'$, and the result $r$ is the same datum on both sides. The input $d$ is arbitrary data, not required to be a well-formed `encode (m, x', y', a, b)`. The hypothesis `hsd : IsSuccinctDesc c n x` is part of the statement, and $x$ enters the conclusion only through `compressedD`. `c`, `x`, `n`, `d`, `r`, `t` are implicit, `lam` is explicit, `G` and `U` are section variables; the proposition is `MIPRE.Halting.haltProg_runs_inv`.

nodes.theorem_title: Size of the compressor's output decider: at most the description size plus a polynomial in the binary length of the level
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`), whose compressed sampler at parameter $\lambda$ is $S^{\mathrm{compr}}_\lambda$ with program computed by the polynomial-time function `G.samplerProg`, and a universal machine $U$ with program `U.univ`. Sizes are node counts of tree encodings: $|a|$ denotes `esize a`, the number of nodes of `encode a`, and $\mathrm{size}(n)$ is the binary length of $n$ (Mathlib's `Nat.size`). At level $n$ the compressor's output carries the parameter $\lambda(n) = 2^{2\,\mathrm{size}(n)}$ and the decider program $\mathrm{outDec}(c, n, \lambda(n))$: the compressor's decider `haltProg G U` with the triple $(c, n, \lambda(n))$ hardcoded. The decider of the verifier this output denotes is the wrapper $\mathrm{wrapCore}(U.\mathrm{univ}, \mathrm{prog}(S^{\mathrm{compr}}_{\lambda(n)}), \mathrm{encode}(\mathrm{outDec}(c, n, \lambda(n))))$, which on an input $(N, x, y, a, b)$ computes the sampler's dimension at $N$ through $U$, checks that $x$ and $y$ have that length, and runs the decider datum on the whole input through $U$, rejecting otherwise. Let $\mathrm{sizeZ}(s) = \mathrm{tb}(8s+5) + 12s + |\mathrm{haltProg}| + 2\,|U.\mathrm{univ}| + \mathrm{wrapNodes} + 43$, where $\mathrm{tb}$ is the polynomial cost bound of `G.samplerProg` and $\mathrm{wrapNodes}$ the fixed node count of the wrapper's skeleton. For every program $c$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$,

$$ \bigl|\mathrm{wrapCore}\bigl(U.\mathrm{univ},\ \mathrm{prog}(S^{\mathrm{compr}}_{\lambda(n)}),\ \mathrm{encode}(\mathrm{outDec}(c, n, \lambda(n)))\bigr)\bigr| \;\le\; |c| + \mathrm{sizeZ}(\mathrm{size}(n)). $$

This is the decider half of the size clause of the output's $n$-boundedness (`Verifier.IsBounded`): beyond the description $c$ it carries, the output's decider has size polynomial in $\log n$, and the slack $2|c| \le n$ of the compressibility criterion is what leaves room for $|c|$.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.esize_wrapCore_le`, with `G : GapCompression` and `U : UniversalMachine` explicit and no hypothesis on `c` or `n`. `lamOf n` unfolds to `2 ^ (2 * Nat.size n)`, `outDec G U c n lam` to `hardcode (haltProg G U) (encode (c, n, lam))`, and `sizeZ G U s` to `G.samplerProg.timeBound.eval (8 * s + 5) + 12 * s + (esize (haltProg G U) + 2 * esize U.univ + wrapNodes + 43)`. The bound is on the raw wrapper program `Prog.wrapCore`, not on the `Verifier` built from it.

nodes.theorem_title: Cost of the compressor's inner decider on a succinct description: the explicit bound innerBound
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix $G$ (`GapCompression`, with polynomial $\mathrm{bound}$, degree $\deg$ and compression map `G.compress`) and $U$ (`UniversalMachine`, with overhead polynomial $U.\mathrm{bound}$); write $|a|$ for `esize a`, the node count of the encoding of $a$, and $\mathrm{size}(k)$ for the binary length of $k$. The pair $(c, n)$ is a succinct description of the bit string $x$ (`IsSuccinctDesc c n x`) when $c$ is a closed program, $|x| \le 2^n$, and for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the program $c$ on the binary input $k$ returns the bit-query answer about $x$ within cost $(n+1)(\mathrm{size}(k)+1)^2$. The inner decider $\mathrm{outDec}(c, n, \lambda)$ is the compressor's decider `haltProg G U` with $(c, n, \lambda)$ hardcoded. `innerBound G U s n L λ l m t` is the explicit natural number $3\,\mathrm{prepBound}(s, n, L, l) + 2(s + 4\,\mathrm{size}(n) + 1 + l + 2) + 3(4\,\mathrm{size}(m) + 1 + t + 1) + U.\mathrm{bound}\bigl(\mathrm{tb}_{\mathrm{compress}}(\mathrm{fBound}(L, n) + l + 2) + (4\,\mathrm{size}(m) + 1 + t + 1) + \mathrm{bound}(m + \lambda)\,(t+1)^{\deg}\bigr) + 15$, where `prepBound` bounds the preparation, $\mathrm{tb}_{\mathrm{compress}}$ is the cost polynomial of `G.compress` and `fBound` bounds the sizes of the frozen programs. For every succinct description $(c, n)$ of $x$, every $\lambda, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and every datum $d$, there exist a result $r$ and a cost $t$ with

$$ t \;\le\; \mathrm{innerBound}\bigl(|c|,\ n,\ |x|,\ \lambda,\ |\lambda|,\ m,\ |d|\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{outDec}(c, n, \lambda)\ \text{on the input}\ \mathrm{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\,m,\ d)\ \text{halts with result}\ r\ \text{at cost}\ t. $$

Per its docstring, the bound is the compressed decider's own time (`GapCompression.decider_time`), simulated by the universal machine, after the preparation; it is the inner cost the wrapper's cost `wrapCoreCost` takes as a parameter.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.outDec_cost`, with `G`, `U` explicit, `c x n` implicit and `hsd : IsSuccinctDesc c n x`; `(outDec G U c n lam).Runs (.cons (encode m) d) r t` means `Eval [cons (encode m) d] (outDec G U c n lam) r t`, a terminating run with result `r` at cost `t`. The result `r` is existential and unconstrained: a halting-and-cost statement only. `d : Data` is arbitrary, `d.size` its node count. The numerals `m` and `n` enter `innerBound` through `4 * Nat.size _ + 1`, the general bound on the `esize` of a natural, which keeps the bound monotone.

nodes.theorem_title: The output decider's wrapper cost is below the master bound decZ at the largest of the index, the level and the input size
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix $G$ (`GapCompression`, with polynomial $\mathrm{bound}$ and degree $\deg$) and $U$ (`UniversalMachine`, with overhead polynomial $U.\mathrm{bound}$); write $|a|$ for `esize a`, $\mathrm{size}(z)$ for the binary length of $z$ and $\lambda(n) = 2^{2\,\mathrm{size}(n)}$. `wrapCoreCost U S dec Cf kf m T s` is the cost of the wrapper `wrapCore` around the decider program `dec` at index $m$ on an input of size $s$, when `dec` runs within $T$ on it and `S` runs within $Cf(m')(|d|+1)^{kf}$ at index $m'$: $(60\,\mathrm{wrapHeadZ}^2 + 4) + 2\,\mathrm{checkCost}(s, \dim_S(m)) + 2(|\mathrm{dec}| + |m| + s + 2) + U.\mathrm{bound}(|\mathrm{dec}| + |m| + s + 1 + T) + 20$, with $\mathrm{checkCost}(E, k) = 60(E + k + 30)^2$ and $\mathrm{wrapHeadZ}$ bounding the head that computes the sampler's dimension. `decZ G U z` is the master bound: the same expression with every atom replaced by its bound in the single variable $z$: the compressed sampler's program size $\sigma(z)$, the inner decider's size $\delta(z)$, the inner cost $\iota(z) = \mathrm{innerBound}(z, z, z+1, \lambda(z), 8\,\mathrm{size}(z)+5, z, z)$, the sampler bound $\mathrm{bound}(z + \lambda(z))$ and the head bound $\mathrm{headZ}(z)$. Let $c$ be a program, $x$ a bit string and $n, m, t, z \in \mathbb{N}$ with $|c| \le n$, $|x| \le n+1$, $m \le z$, $n \le z$ and $t \le z$. Then

$$ \mathrm{wrapCoreCost}\Bigl(U,\ S^{\mathrm{compr}}_{\lambda(n)},\ \mathrm{outDec}(c, n, \lambda(n)),\ m' \mapsto \mathrm{bound}(m' + \lambda(n)),\ \deg,\ m,\ \mathrm{innerBound}(|c|, n, |x|, \lambda(n), |\lambda(n)|, m, t),\ t\Bigr) \;\le\; \mathrm{decZ}(z). $$

The single variable is the point: the output decider's cost at index $m$, level $n$ and input size $t$ is dominated by one polynomially bounded function of $\max(m, n, t)$, the form the absorption lemmas of `Halting/Absorb.lean` turn into the clause $m^n (|d|+1)^n$ of $n$-boundedness.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.wrapCoreCost_le_decZ`, with `G`, `U` explicit and `c x n m t z` implicit, fixed by the hypotheses `hc hx hm hn ht`. No succinctness hypothesis and no run appear: both sides are closed arithmetic expressions over ℕ (`wrapCoreCost`, `innerBound`, `decZ` and its atoms `headZ`, `sampZ`, `sigZ`, `deltaZ`, `iotaZ` are definitions evaluating polynomials over ℕ). The sampler's coefficient function is the literal `fun m => G.bound.eval (m + lamOf n)` and its degree `G.deg`, the data of `GapCompression.sampler_time`.

nodes.theorem_title: Decider clause of the compressor's output: past a threshold, the output's decider runs within $m^n (|d|+1)^n$ at every index $m \ge 2$
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix $G$ (`GapCompression`) and $U$ (`UniversalMachine`), and write $|a|$ for `esize a` (the node count of the encoding) and $\mathrm{size}(k)$ for the binary length of $k$. On $(c, n)$ the compressor outputs the string $\mathrm{comprStr}(c, n, \lambda(n))$: the postorder serialization of the pair of the parameter $\lambda(n) = 2^{2\,\mathrm{size}(n)}$ and the decider program $\mathrm{outDec}(c, n, \lambda(n))$, the compressor's decider `haltProg G U` with $(c, n, \lambda(n))$ hardcoded. A string $y$ denotes the verifier $\mathrm{Vof}(y)$: the compressed sampler at the parameter the string carries, and the string's decider datum run by $U$ inside the question-length wrapper (`Decider.wrap`). For a decider $\mathcal{D}$, `TimeBoundAt m T k` says that for every datum $d$ the program of $\mathcal{D}$ halts on the input $\mathrm{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\,m, d)$ within cost $T(|d|+1)^k$. The pair $(c, n)$ is a succinct description of $x$ (`IsSuccinctDesc c n x`) when $c$ is closed, $|x| \le 2^n$ and $c$ answers every bit query $k$ about $x$ within cost $(n+1)(\mathrm{size}(k)+1)^2$. There is a threshold $n_0$, depending on $G$ and $U$ alone, such that for all $n \ge n_0$, all programs $c$ and bit strings $x$ with $2|c| \le n$, $(c, n)$ a succinct description of $x$ and $|x| \le n+1$, and every index $m \ge 2$:

$$ \forall d \in \mathrm{Data}:\qquad \text{the decider of } \mathrm{Vof}\bigl(\mathrm{comprStr}(c, n, \lambda(n))\bigr) \text{ halts on } \mathrm{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\,m,\ d) \text{ within cost } m^{n}\,(|d|+1)^{n}. $$

This is the decider clause of `Verifier.IsBounded n` for the output's verifier, the third of its per-index clauses (dimension, sampler time, decider time); with the sampler and size clauses it yields the field `CompressorSpec.isBounded_compr`, the accounting half of obligation O4.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.decider_clause`, with `G`, `U` explicit. The conclusion `(Vof G U (comprStr G U c n (lamOf n))).decider.TimeBoundAt m (m ^ n) n` unfolds to `∀ d : Data, HaltsWithin prog (.cons (encode m) d) (m ^ n * (d.size + 1) ^ n)`, with `HaltsWithin p x t := ∃ r t', t' ≤ t ∧ Eval [x] p r t'`: `d` ranges over all data, well formed or not, and nothing is said about the result. The threshold is existential; `2 * esize c ≤ n` and `x.length ≤ n + 1` are the slack and the length bound the compressibility criterion provides; the bound is in `m` and `n`, not in `λ(n)`.

nodes.theorem_title: Growth of the parameter $\lambda(n) = 2^{2\,\mathrm{size}(n)}$: the field lam_ge of the compressor's specification
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $\lambda(n) = 2^{2\,\mathrm{size}(n)}$ (`lamOf n`), where $\mathrm{size}(n)$ is the binary length of $n$ (Mathlib's `Nat.size`): in binary, a $1$ followed by $2\,\mathrm{size}(n)$ zeros, so that the compressor can write it down in time polynomial in $\log n$. Write $|k|$ for `esize k`, the node count of the encoding of $k \in \mathbb{N}$ as the list of its binary digits (at most $4\,\mathrm{size}(k)+1$). There is a threshold $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$,

$$ (2n+1)^{2n+1} + |2n+1| + 4 \;\le\; 2^{\lambda(n)} \qquad\text{and}\qquad 2n+1 + |2n+1| + 53 \;\le\; \lambda(n). $$

These are the two inequalities the field `CompressorSpec.lam_ge` asks of the parameter, in the form `Verifier.freeze_isBounded` consumes: a $(2n+1)$-bounded verifier has, at index $2n+1$, dimension and running-time coefficients at most $(2n+1)^{2n+1}$ and size at most $2n+1$; freezing it at that index adds $|2n+1| + 4$ to the running times and $|2n+1| + 53$ to the size, and the frozen verifier is $\lambda(n)$-bounded once these fit under $2^{\lambda(n)}$ and $\lambda(n)$. It is blueprint `lem:lambda`, the choice of the parameter of the halting verifier, in the per-level form of the formalization, where the boundedness parameter is tied to the level.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.lamOf_ge`; it mentions neither `G` nor `U`, so it takes no argument, and it is arithmetic over ℕ. `lamOf n` unfolds to `2 ^ (2 * Nat.size n)` and `esize (2 * n + 1)` to `(encode (2 * n + 1) : Data).size`, the encoding of a natural being its `Nat.bits` (least significant first) as a `cons`-chain of bits. The constants $4$ and $53$ are the freezing overheads of `Halting/Freeze.lean` (`freeze_timeBoundAt`, `freeze_size`). The threshold is existential; the module docstring records that $\lambda(n) \ge (n+1)^2$ is what freezing at index $2n+1$ needs.

nodes.theorem_title: The compressor meets its specification: a polynomial-time program for $(c, n) \mapsto \mathrm{comprStr}(c, n, \lambda(n))$ yields a CompressorSpec
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix $G$ (`GapCompression`, with constant $C_0$, compressed samplers, output verifiers `G.output` and polynomial $\mathrm{bound}$) and $U$ (`UniversalMachine`); write $|a|$ for `esize a`. `CompressorSpec G U` is the specification of the compressor of the halting reduction: a threshold $n_0 \ge C_0$; a polynomial-time function `compr : PolyTimeFun (Prog × ℕ) BitStr` (a function with a closed program computing it on encodings and an explicit polynomial cost bound); a parameter `lam : ℕ → ℕ`; and five properties, all for $n \ge n_0$. `descLam_compr`: `compr (c, n)` carries the parameter `lam n`. `accepts_compr`: for $2|c| \le n$, $(c, n)$ a succinct description of $x$ and $|x| \le n+1$, the decider of `Vof (compr (c, n))` accepts, at every index and on all questions and answers, exactly what the compressed decider `G.output` of the verifier of $x$ frozen at index $2n+1$, at parameter `lam n`, accepts. `isBounded_compr`: under the same hypotheses, if `Vof x` is $(2n+1)$-bounded then `Vof (compr (c, n))` is $n$-bounded. `lam_ge`: $(2n+1)^{2n+1} + |2n+1| + 4 \le 2^{\mathrm{lam}\,n}$ and $2n+1 + |2n+1| + 53 \le \mathrm{lam}\,n$. `ansBound_le`: for $|x| \le n+1$, $\mathrm{ansBound}(x, 2n+1) \le (2^n)^{\mathrm{lam}\,n}$. Let `compr` be a polynomial-time function with $\mathrm{compr}(c, n) = \mathrm{comprStr}(c, n, \lambda(n))$ for all $c, n$, where $\lambda(n) = 2^{2\,\mathrm{size}(n)}$ and `comprStr G U c n lam` is the string denoting the parameter `lam` and the decider `haltProg G U` with $(c, n, \mathrm{lam})$ hardcoded. Then

$$ \exists\, S : \mathrm{CompressorSpec}(G, U):\qquad S.\mathrm{compr} = \mathrm{compr}\ \ \wedge\ \ S.\mathrm{lam} = \lambda. $$

A `CompressorSpec` yields `Obligations G U` by the class transfer `CompressorSpec.toObligations`, and `Obligations` is all the halting reduction assumes beyond a gap compression and a universal machine; the program itself (`comprPoly` of `Halting/CompressorProgram.lean`) supplies the hypothesis.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.exists_compressorSpec`, with `G`, `U`, `compr` and `hcompr : ∀ c n, compr (c, n) = comprStr G U c n (lamOf n)` explicit; `compr (c, n)` is the `PolyTimeFun` coerced to its underlying function. The conclusion fixes the two data fields `compr` and `lam = lamOf` of the witness and leaves its threshold `n₀` existential.

nodes.theorem_title: Halting reduction from gap-preserving compression, in both values: synchronous and quantum value 1 on halting machines, at most 1/2 otherwise
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Computation is Mathlib's: a machine is a code $\mathcal{M}$ (`Nat.Partrec.Code`), halting on the empty input when $\mathcal{M}.\mathrm{eval}(0)$ is defined (`HaltsOnEmptyInput`), and maps are `Computable`. A game description $d$ (`GameData`), two naturals $n_X, n_A$ and two finite lists of natural-number weights on question pairs and of accepted tuples, denotes the synchronous game $d.\mathrm{toGame}$ on questions $\mathrm{Fin}(n_X+1)$ and answers $\mathrm{Fin}(n_A+1)$ whose distribution normalizes the weights (a point mass on $(0,0)$ when the total weight is $0$) and whose predicate accepts the listed tuples, unequal answers to equal questions always losing. $\mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(d)$ (`gameValue d.toGame`) is the supremum over synchronous strategies (one projective measurement family for both players, measured in the tracial state $\mathrm{Tr}(\cdot)/\dim$) of the winning probability; $\mathrm{val}^*(d)$ (`quantumValue d.game`) is the supremum over finite-dimensional tensor-product strategies of the same game read as a two-player game. Assume a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`, blueprint `thm:compression`) and a universal machine $U$. Then there is one computable map $g$ from codes to game descriptions such that for every code $\mathcal{M}$:

$$ \bigl(\mathcal{M} \text{ halts on } \varepsilon \Rightarrow \mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(g(\mathcal{M})) = 1 \wedge \mathrm{val}^*(g(\mathcal{M})) = 1\bigr) \ \wedge\ \bigl(\mathcal{M} \text{ does not halt on } \varepsilon \Rightarrow \mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(g(\mathcal{M})) \le \tfrac12 \wedge \mathrm{val}^*(g(\mathcal{M})) \le \tfrac12\bigr). $$

The two headline statements, `halting_reduces_to_gameValue_of` (blueprint `thm:main`, synchronous value) and `halting_reduction_quantum_of` (`cor:main-quantum`, quantum value), are its two projections, on the same map.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.halting_reduction_both_of`, with `G : GapCompression` and `U : UniversalMachine` as explicit arguments (`include G U`): it is conditional on an instance of the compression theorem, which `MIPRE/MainTheorem.lean` supplies separately. `HaltsOnEmptyInput pc` unfolds to `(pc.eval 0).Dom`; `1 / 2` is the real one half; `GameData.game` is `d.toGame` repackaged as a `MIPRE.Game` with the same distribution and predicate; `Computable g` uses the `Primcodable` instance of `GameData` as a tuple. Only computability of `g` is claimed, no time bound.

nodes.theorem_title: Halting reduces to the synchronous game value, from gap-preserving compression (the main theorem, conditional on compression)
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Computation is Mathlib's: a machine is a code $\mathcal{M}$ (`Nat.Partrec.Code`), halting on the empty input when $\mathcal{M}.\mathrm{eval}(0)$ is defined (`HaltsOnEmptyInput`), and maps are `Computable`. A game description $d$ (`GameData`) is a first-order tuple of two naturals $n_X, n_A$, a list of natural-number weights on question pairs and a list of accepted tuples; it denotes the synchronous game $d.\mathrm{toGame}$ on questions $\mathrm{Fin}(n_X+1)$ and answers $\mathrm{Fin}(n_A+1)$: the weights normalized (a point mass on $(0,0)$ when the total weight is $0$), the listed tuples accepted, unequal answers to equal questions always rejected. Its synchronous value $\mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(d)$ (`gameValue d.toGame`) is the supremum, over synchronous strategies (a single question-indexed projective measurement family on $\mathbb{C}^k$, shared by both players and measured in the tracial state $\mathrm{Tr}(\cdot)/k$), of the winning probability. Assume a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`) and a universal machine $U$. Then there is a computable map $g$ from codes to game descriptions such that for every code $\mathcal{M}$,

$$ \bigl(\mathcal{M} \text{ halts on } \varepsilon \ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(g(\mathcal{M})) = 1\bigr)\ \ \wedge\ \ \bigl(\mathcal{M} \text{ does not halt on } \varepsilon \ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(g(\mathcal{M})) \le \tfrac12\bigr). $$

This is blueprint `thm:main` from `thm:compression`: the proposition `HaltingGameValue.HaltingReducesToGameValue`, the self-contained statement of the main theorem written on top of Mathlib alone, with the compression theorem as a hypothesis. Per the docstring, `MIPRE/MainTheorem.lean` supplies the compression and proves the unconditional statement `HaltingGameValue.halting_reduces_to_gameValue`.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.halting_reduces_to_gameValue_of`, with `G : GapCompression` and `U : UniversalMachine` as explicit arguments (`include G U`); it is the synchronous-value projection of `halting_reduction_both_of`, on the same map. `HaltsOnEmptyInput pc` unfolds to `(pc.eval 0).Dom`; `1 / 2` is the real one half; `gameValue` is the `iSup` of the strategy values over all `SyncStrategy` of the game. Only computability of `g` is claimed, no polynomial-time bound.

nodes.theorem_title: Halting reduces to the quantum (tensor-product) value of a described game, from gap-preserving compression
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Computation is Mathlib's: a machine is a code $\mathcal{M}$ (`Nat.Partrec.Code`), halting on the empty input when $\mathcal{M}.\mathrm{eval}(0)$ is defined (`HaltsOnEmptyInput`), and maps are `Computable`. A game description $d$ (`GameData`) is a tuple of two naturals $n_X, n_A$, a list of natural-number weights on question pairs and a list of accepted tuples; `d.game` is the two-player game it denotes, on questions $\mathrm{Fin}(n_X+1)$ for both players and answers $\mathrm{Fin}(n_A+1)$, with the weights normalized (a point mass on $(0,0)$ when the total weight is $0$), the listed tuples accepted and unequal answers to equal questions rejected. Its quantum value $\mathrm{val}^*(d)$ (`quantumValue d.game`) is the supremum over tensor-product strategies, finite-dimensional spaces $\mathbb{C}^{d_A} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{d_B}$ with a unit vector $\psi$ and projective measurements $\{A^x_a\}$, $\{B^y_b\}$, of the Born-rule winning probability $\sum \mu(x,y)\,[D(x,y,a,b)]\,\langle \psi | A^x_a \otimes B^y_b | \psi \rangle$. Assume a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`) and a universal machine $U$. Then there is a computable map $g$ from codes to game descriptions such that for every code $\mathcal{M}$,

$$ \bigl(\mathcal{M} \text{ halts on } \varepsilon \ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{val}^*(g(\mathcal{M})) = 1\bigr)\ \ \wedge\ \ \bigl(\mathcal{M} \text{ does not halt on } \varepsilon \ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{val}^*(g(\mathcal{M})) \le \tfrac12\bigr). $$

Per the docstring this is blueprint `cor:main-quantum`, on the same map as `thm:main`: the quantum value replaces the synchronous value. It is the form the class `MIPStarComputable` is defined with, the one `re_subset_mipstarComputable_of` composes with.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.halting_reduction_quantum_of`, with `G : GapCompression` and `U : UniversalMachine` as explicit arguments (`include G U`); it is the quantum-value projection of `halting_reduction_both_of`, on the same map. `HaltsOnEmptyInput pc` unfolds to `(pc.eval 0).Dom`; `1 / 2` is the real one half; `GameData.game` is `d.toGame` repackaged as a `MIPRE.Game` with the same distribution and predicate, and `quantumValue` is the `iSup` of `TensorProductStrategy.value` over all tensor-product strategies, whose measurements are projective (no loss of generality by Naimark dilation, per the docstring of `TensorProductStrategy`). Only computability of `g` is claimed.

nodes.theorem_title: Uncomputability of the synchronous value under the promise value 1 or at most 1/2, conditionally on compression
nodes.natural_language_statement:
A game description $d$ (`GameData`), a tuple of two naturals $n_X, n_A$, a list of natural-number weights on question pairs and a list of accepted tuples, denotes the synchronous game $d.\mathrm{toGame}$ on questions $\mathrm{Fin}(n_X+1)$ and answers $\mathrm{Fin}(n_A+1)$: the weights normalized, with a point mass on $(0,0)$ when the total weight is $0$; the listed tuples accepted; unequal answers to equal questions rejected. Its synchronous value $\mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(d)$ (`gameValue d.toGame`) is the supremum over synchronous strategies (one shared projective measurement family measured in the tracial state) of the winning probability. `GameData` is `Primcodable`, so a map $f : \mathrm{GameData} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is computable in Mathlib's sense (`Computable f`). Assume a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`) and a universal machine $U$. Then no computable $f$ answers $\mathrm{true}$ on every description of synchronous value $1$ and $\mathrm{false}$ on every description of synchronous value at most $\tfrac12$:

$$ \neg\,\exists\, f : \mathrm{GameData} \to \mathrm{Bool}\ \text{computable}:\quad \bigl(\forall d,\ \mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(d) = 1 \Rightarrow f(d) = \mathrm{true}\bigr)\ \wedge\ \bigl(\forall d,\ \mathrm{val}_{\mathrm{sync}}(d) \le \tfrac12 \Rightarrow f(d) = \mathrm{false}\bigr). $$

This is blueprint `cor:value-uncomputable`, first clause: the promise problem of deciding whether the synchronous value of a described game is $1$ or at most $\tfrac12$ is undecidable. Nothing is required of $f$ on descriptions whose value lies strictly between $\tfrac12$ and $1$.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.gameValue_uncomputable_of`, with `G : GapCompression` and `U : UniversalMachine` as explicit arguments (`include G U`): the result is conditional on compression, as the halting reduction it rests on. `f` returns Lean's `Bool`, and the two clauses are implications, not an equivalence, so the statement is the undecidability of a promise problem; `1 / 2` is the real one half, and `gameValue` is the `iSup` over `SyncStrategy`.

Per the module docstring, the same module proves Turing's theorem, `halting_undecidable`, from Mathlib's `ComputablePred.halting_problem` at the empty input.

nodes.theorem_title: Every recursively enumerable language many-one reduces to halting on the empty input
nodes.natural_language_statement:
A language is a set $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ of bit strings (`Set BitStr`, with `BitStr = List Bool`); it is recursively enumerable, `IsRE L`, when membership $x \mapsto (x \in L)$ is an `REPred` in Mathlib's sense, the domain of a partial computable function. A code is an element of Mathlib's `Nat.Partrec.Code`, the Gödel numbering of partial recursive functions; a code $e$ halts on the empty input (`HaltsOnEmptyInput e`) when $e.\mathrm{eval}(0)$ is defined. Then for every recursively enumerable $L$ there is a computable map $r$ from bit strings to codes such that

$$ \forall x \in \{0,1\}^*:\qquad r(x) \text{ halts on the empty input} \iff x \in L. $$

Per its docstring, the map fixes the string into a code for the enumerator of $L$ by Mathlib's `Nat.Partrec.Code.curry`. The theorem is the many-one reduction that `re_subset_mipstarComputable_of` composes with the halting reduction to obtain $\mathrm{RE} \subseteq \mathrm{MIP}^*$; it belongs to the formalization of blueprint `thm:halting-undecidable` (Turing), the chapter 3 background result on the halting problem.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.exists_code_halts_of_isRE`, with `L : Set BitStr` implicit and `h : IsRE L` explicit; it mentions neither `G` nor `U` and is unconditional, a statement about Mathlib's computability alone. `IsRE L` unfolds to `REPred (· ∈ L)` and `HaltsOnEmptyInput c` to `(c.eval 0).Dom`; `Computable r` is for the `Primcodable` instances of `BitStr` (as `List Bool`) and of `Code`. The equivalence is exact in both directions, for every string.
