nodes.theorem_title: RE is contained in MIP* (computable version), conditionally on gap-preserving compression
nodes.natural_language_statement:
A language $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ is recursively enumerable, `IsRE L`, when membership is an `REPred`: the domain of a partial computable function. `MIPStarComputable L` is the computable form of the class $\mathrm{MIP}^*$ (blueprint `def:mipstar`): there is a computable map $g$ from bit strings to game descriptions (`GameData`, two naturals and two finite lists denoting a game on $\mathrm{Fin}(n_X+1)$ questions and $\mathrm{Fin}(n_A+1)$ answers) such that the quantum value $\mathrm{val}^*(g(x))$ (`quantumValue (g x).game`, the supremum over finite-dimensional tensor-product strategies of the winning probability) is $1$ when $x \in L$ and at most $\tfrac12$ when $x \notin L$. Assume a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`) and a universal machine $U$. Then every recursively enumerable language is in the class:

$$ \mathrm{IsRE}(L)\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists\, g : \{0,1\}^* \to \mathrm{GameData}\ \text{computable}:\ \forall x,\ \bigl(x \in L \Rightarrow \mathrm{val}^*(g(x)) = 1\bigr) \wedge \bigl(x \notin L \Rightarrow \mathrm{val}^*(g(x)) \le \tfrac12\bigr). $$

Per the docstring, it composes the many-one reduction of $L$ to halting on the empty input with the halting reduction of `cor:main-quantum`. It is the hard half of blueprint `thm:mipstar-eq-re`; the other half, `MIPStarComputable.isRE`, is unconditional.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.re_subset_mipstarComputable_of`, with `G`, `U` explicit (`include G U`), `L` implicit and `h : IsRE L`; the conclusion is the predicate `MIPStarComputable L`, which unfolds to the displayed existential. The class is the computable one, with games given as explicit descriptions and only `Computable g` asked, not a polynomial-time verifier; the module docstring of `ClassMIPStarComputable.lean` records that the paper's class is contained in it. `1 / 2` is the real one half.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 5 lines long and reduces to two platform theorems: `MIPRE.Halting.exists_code_halts_of_isRE` (the many-one reduction of an r.e. language to halting on the empty input) and `MIPRE.Halting.halting_reduction_quantum_of` (the halting reduction in the quantum value); it pastes no helper lemma from the source modules.

nodes.theorem_title: MIP* = RE as predicates on languages (computable version), conditionally on gap-preserving compression
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Languages are sets $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ of bit strings. `IsRE L` says $L$ is recursively enumerable: membership is an `REPred`, the domain of a partial computable function in Mathlib's computability. `MIPStarComputable L` says $L$ is in the computable form of $\mathrm{MIP}^*$ (blueprint `def:mipstar`): there is a computable map $g$ from bit strings to game descriptions (`GameData`) whose quantum value $\mathrm{val}^*(g(x))$ (`quantumValue (g x).game`, the supremum over finite-dimensional tensor-product strategies of the winning probability) is $1$ when $x \in L$ and at most $\tfrac12$ when $x \notin L$. Assume a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`, the hypothesis structure of blueprint `thm:compression`) and a universal machine $U$. Then the two classes coincide:

$$ \mathrm{MIPStarComputable} \;=\; \mathrm{IsRE} \qquad\text{as predicates on } L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*,\ \text{that is,}\ \ \forall L,\ \mathrm{MIPStarComputable}(L) \iff \mathrm{IsRE}(L). $$

This is blueprint `thm:mipstar-eq-re`, the statement $\mathrm{MIP}^* = \mathrm{RE}$, in the form the formalization uses: the inclusion $\mathrm{MIP}^* \subseteq \mathrm{RE}$ is `MIPStarComputable.isRE`, unconditional, obtained by enumerating strategies and accepting upon finding one of value above $\tfrac12$; the inclusion $\mathrm{RE} \subseteq \mathrm{MIP}^*$ is `re_subset_mipstarComputable_of`, conditional on compression.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.mipstarComputable_eq_re_of`, with `G`, `U` explicit (`include G U`); it is an equality of two functions `Set BitStr → Prop`, so function extensionality and propositional extensionality are part of its meaning. The class is the computable one (games as explicit descriptions, `Computable g`), which per the module docstring of `ClassMIPStarComputable.lean` contains the paper's polynomial-time class. `1 / 2` is the real one half.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 1 line long and reduces to one platform theorem, `MIPRE.Halting.re_subset_mipstarComputable_of` (the inclusion of RE in MIP*); it pastes 1 helper lemma from the source modules into the uploaded file. Per the module docstring, the other inclusion is `MIPStarComputable.isRE`, the unconditional containment of MIP* in RE proved in `ClassMIPStarComputable.lean`.

nodes.theorem_title: Decoding a bit string from data succeeds only on its encoding
nodes.natural_language_statement:
The ambient model computes on binary trees: `Data` has the two constructors `nil` and `cons a b`. A bit is encoded as $\mathrm{false} \mapsto \mathrm{nil}$, $\mathrm{true} \mapsto \mathrm{cons}(\mathrm{nil}, \mathrm{nil})$, and a bit string $l \in \{0,1\}^*$ (`BitStr = List Bool`) as the `cons`-chain of its bits ending in `nil`, so $\mathrm{encode}(l) = \mathrm{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\,l_0, \mathrm{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\,l_1, \ldots \mathrm{nil}))$. Decoding, `decode : Data → Option BitStr`, reads the chain back elementwise: `nil` decodes to the empty string, `cons a d` to $b :: l$ when $a$ decodes to the bit $b$ and $d$ to $l$, and to `none` whenever a cell is neither `nil` nor `cons nil nil`. The class `SizedEncoding` guarantees $\mathrm{decode}(\mathrm{encode}\,l) = \mathrm{some}\,l$; this theorem is the converse: for every datum $d$ and bit string $l$,

$$ \mathrm{decode}(d) = \mathrm{some}(l) \ \Longrightarrow\ \mathrm{encode}(l) = d. $$

So decoding is injective where it succeeds, and the data on which it succeeds are exactly the encodings of bit strings. The descriptions of the halting reduction travel as bit strings and their parameters as binary numerals read back from data; `encode_natOf` uses this to show that a normalized parameter is the encoding of the number it denotes.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Data.encode_of_decode_bitStr`, with `d : Data` and `l : BitStr` implicit and `h : (decode d : Option BitStr) = some l`; `decode` and `encode` are those of the `SizedEncoding BitStr` instance, `Data.toList? Data.toBool?` and `Data.ofList Data.ofBool`. The type ascription `(decode d : Option BitStr)` selects the bit-string instance, as `Data` also decodes to naturals and pairs. No size or well-formedness hypothesis is needed.
nodes.source: https://github.com/vidick/MIPRE-formalization/blob/70cbf1c52e3d5e1dff1162fdf952c9a9f4bd99ed/MIPRE/Foundations/Halting/Descriptions.lean#L141-L170; internal lemma of the formalization of blueprint rem:compression-abstract, item 1 (descriptions as bit strings), used in thm:halting, https://vidick.github.io/MIPRE-formalization/blueprint/

nodes.theorem_title: The normalized parameter of a datum is the binary encoding of the number it denotes
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Data are binary trees (`nil`, `cons`); a natural number $n$ is encoded as the list of its binary digits `Nat.bits n` (least significant first, with no trailing zero), each bit as $\mathrm{false} \mapsto \mathrm{nil}$, $\mathrm{true} \mapsto \mathrm{cons}(\mathrm{nil},\mathrm{nil})$ and the list as a `cons`-chain ending in `nil`; a datum decodes to a natural (`decode : Data → Option ℕ`) by decoding it as a bit string and folding `Nat.bit` over the result. A datum $d$ is a canonical binary numeral (`isCanonBin d`) when it decodes to a bit string that is empty or ends in $\mathrm{true}$. The total normalization is $\mathrm{normBin}(d) = d$ if $d$ is canonical and $\mathrm{nil}$ (the encoding of $0$) otherwise, and the number a datum denotes is $\mathrm{natOf}(d)$, the decoding of $\mathrm{normBin}(d)$ as a natural, with default $0$. For every datum $d$,

$$ \mathrm{encode}\bigl(\mathrm{natOf}(d)\bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{normBin}(d). $$

Every string of the compressibility criterion names a parameter through `natOf` applied to the left component of the datum it parses to (`descLam`), with no validity condition on strings; this theorem says the normalized datum is the encoding of that parameter, which is what bounds the parameter by the datum's size (`natOf_lt`, hence `descLam_lt`), the fact the answer budget of the halting reduction depends on.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Data.encode_natOf`, with `d : Data` explicit and the ascription `(encode (natOf d) : Data)` selecting the `SizedEncoding ℕ` instance. `normBin d` unfolds to `if isCanonBin d then d else nil` and `natOf d` to `((decode (normBin d) : Option ℕ)).getD 0`; both are total, every non-canonical datum reading as `0` with `normBin d = nil = encode 0`. `isCanonBin` is a `Bool` computed from `(decode d : Option BitStr)`.

nodes.theorem_title: One step of the postorder stack machine increases the total size on the stack by at most one
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Data are binary trees (`nil`, `cons a b`) with $\mathrm{size}$ the number of nodes, `nil` counting one. A datum is serialized in postorder, $\mathrm{nil} \mapsto 0$ and $\mathrm{cons}(a,b) \mapsto a \cdot b \cdot 1$ (`Data.toBitsPost`), and read back by a stack machine whose step `stackStep s bit` on a stack $s$ (a list of data, top first) is: on the bit $0$, push `nil`; on the bit $1$ with at least two entries, pop $b$ then $a$ and push $\mathrm{cons}(a, b)$; on the bit $1$ with fewer than two entries, leave the stack unchanged. For every stack $s$ and bit $b$,

$$ \sum_{e \in \mathrm{stackStep}(s, b)} \mathrm{size}(e) \;\le\; \sum_{e \in s} \mathrm{size}(e) + 1. $$

A $0$ adds a node of size one; a $1$ replaces two entries of sizes $\sigma_a, \sigma_b$ by one of size $\sigma_a + \sigma_b + 1$, or does nothing. Summed over a run, the total size on the stack after reading a string is at most its length, which is how the datum a string parses to is bounded by the string's length (`size_parse_le`) and, through `natOf_lt`, how a short description names a small parameter.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Data.size_sum_stackStep_le`, with `s : List Data` and `bit : Bool` explicit; the sums are `((stackStep s bit).map size).sum` and `(s.map size).sum` over ℕ. `stackStep` is total: the degenerate case of a `1` on a stack with fewer than two entries is covered, and the pop reads the top two entries with `head?.getD nil`, which the length test makes exact. The bound is on one step alone; the run `stackRun` is `List.foldl stackStep`.

nodes.theorem_title: Freezing a verifier at an index preserves perfect PCC strategies: the frozen verifier has one at any index iff the original has one at the frozen index
nodes.natural_language_statement:
A normal-form verifier $V$ with $\ell$ levels (`Verifier ℓ`) is a sampler and a decider, two programs of the ambient model; at index $n$ its game $\mathcal{V}_n$ with answers of length at most $T$ (`V.game n T`) has questions $\mathbb{F}_2^{s(n)}$, with $s(n)$ the sampler's dimension, distributed as the sampler prescribes, and accepts $(x, y, a, b)$ when the decider accepts $(n, x, y, a, b)$. The doubled game `V.doubledGame n T` plays on $\mathrm{Bool} \times \mathbb{F}_2^{s(n)}$: the pair $((\mathrm{false}, x), (\mathrm{true}, y))$ has the weight of $(x, y)$ and is decided as $(x, y)$ is, every other pair has weight zero and is rejected; it is a synchronous game for every $V$. $V$ has a perfect PCC strategy at index $n$ and answer bound $T$ (`V.HasPerfectPCC n T`) when some synchronous strategy of the doubled game, a single family of projective measurements played by both players and measured in the tracial state, is PCC (commuting on the support of the question distribution) and has value $1$. The verifier frozen at index $k$, `V.freeze k`, has sampler and decider programs that, on any input $(N, d)$, run the original programs on $(k, d)$: at every index it presents the dimension, the CL functions and the acceptance of $V$ at index $k$. For all $k, n, T \in \mathbb{N}$,

$$ \mathrm{HasPerfectPCC}\bigl(V^{\mathrm{frz}\,k},\ n,\ T\bigr)\ \iff\ \mathrm{HasPerfectPCC}(V,\ k,\ T). $$

Freezing is item 2 of blueprint `rem:compression-abstract`: the compressibility criterion recurses $n \to 2n+1$ while gap-preserving compression relates the game at index $2^n$ to the output at index $n$, and freezing the described verifier at $2n+1$ before compressing reconciles the two, the frozen verifier's game at index $2^n$ being the original's at level $2n+1$. This theorem is the transfer of perfect PCC strategies across that step, the companion of `freeze_valStar` for the value.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Verifier.freeze_hasPerfectPCC`, with `ℓ` implicit and `V : Verifier ℓ`, `k n T` explicit. `HasPerfectPCC n T` unfolds to `∃ S : SyncStrategy (V.doubledGame n T), S.IsPCC ∧ S.value = 1`; `V.freeze k` has `sampler := V.sampler.freeze k` and `decider := V.decider.freeze k`, both with programs `Prog.freezeProg k _`, and `(V.freeze k).sampler.dim n = V.sampler.dim k` definitionally, so the two question types agree. The equivalence holds at every `n`, with no boundedness or synchronicity hypothesis.

nodes.theorem_title: The answer budget of level 2n+1 fits under the compression theorem's budget $(2^n)^\lambda$, for short strings and large parameters
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`), with the polynomial $\mathrm{bound} \in \mathbb{N}[X]$ that bounds the running times of its outputs and the length of the answers its compressed deciders accept: at index $n$ and parameter $\lambda$ the compressed decider accepts no answer longer than $\mathrm{bound}(n + \lambda)$. A bit string $x$ denotes a description: it parses (`Data.parse`, the postorder stack machine) to a datum whose left component, normalized to a canonical binary numeral, is the parameter $\lambda_x = \mathrm{descLam}(x) \in \mathbb{N}$ the string carries; every string carries one. The answer budget the classes of the halting reduction are read with at level $n$ is $\mathrm{ansBound}(x, n) = \mathrm{bound}(n + \lambda_x)$. There are thresholds $\lambda_0, n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$, depending on $G$ alone, such that for every bit string $x$ and all $\lambda, n$ with $\lambda \ge \lambda_0$, $n \ge n_0$ and $|x| \le n + 1$,

$$ \mathrm{ansBound}(x,\ 2n+1) \;=\; \mathrm{bound}\bigl(2n + 1 + \lambda_x\bigr) \;\le\; \bigl(2^{n}\bigr)^{\lambda}. $$

Per its docstring, $(2^n)^\lambda$ is the answer bound at which `GapCompression.completeness` takes its hypothesis, so this inequality (with `Verifier.hasPerfectPCC_of_le`) carries a value-$1$ PCC strategy from membership in the class $A$ at level $2n+1$ into that clause; it is why `Obligations.compr_spec` carries the length bound $|x| \le n+1$: the budget grows with the string's own parameter, and without a bound on it no thresholds would do. The docstring records the witnesses $\lambda_0 = 2\deg(\mathrm{bound}) + 1$ and $n_0 = \log_2\|\mathrm{bound}\| + 2\deg(\mathrm{bound}) + 1$, with $\|\mathrm{bound}\|$ the sum of the coefficients; they are set by the polynomial, not by `G.deg`.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.exists_ansBound_le`, with `G : GapCompression` explicit and no universal machine involved. `ansBound G x n` unfolds to `G.bound.eval (n + descLam x)` and `descLam x` to `Data.natOf (Data.parse x).left`, both total on arbitrary strings; `(2 ^ n) ^ lam` is in ℕ. The thresholds are existential in the statement; the explicit values above are the docstring's. The field `CompressorSpec.ansBound_le` is this statement at `lam = lamOf n` with a single threshold.

Per the docstring, the thresholds are set by the polynomial `G.bound`, not by `G.deg`.

nodes.theorem_title: The μ clause of the tabulation: the tabulated question distribution is the doubled game's, under the question relabeling
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix $G$ (`GapCompression`) and $U$ (`UniversalMachine`). A bit string $x$ denotes the verifier $\mathrm{Vof}(x)$: the compressed sampler at the parameter $\lambda_x = \mathrm{descLam}(x)$ it carries, and its decider datum run by $U$ inside the question-length wrapper. Its game $\mathcal{V}_n$ at index $n$ has questions $\mathbb{F}_2^{s(n)}$, $s(n)$ the sampler's dimension, distributed as the sampler prescribes. With the answer budget $T = \mathrm{ansBound}(x, n) = \mathrm{bound}(n + \lambda_x)$, the doubled game `(Vof x).doubledGame n T` plays on $\mathrm{Bool} \times \mathbb{F}_2^{s(n)}$, giving $((\mathrm{false}, p), (\mathrm{true}, q))$ weight $\mu_{\mathcal{V}_n}(p, q)$ and every other pair weight $0$. The tabulation `tab G U x n` is a game description (`GameData`) of this doubled game, its sampler runs budgeted by the compressed sampler's own time bound; `(tab G U x n).game` is the game it denotes, on $n_X + 1 = 2^{s(n)+1}$ question indices, with $\mu(i, j)$ the weight of $(i, j)$ over the total weight (a point mass on $(0,0)$ if that total is $0$). The relabeling $e_X = \mathrm{eXof}(x, n)$ is the bijection from these indices to $\mathrm{Bool} \times \mathbb{F}_2^{s(n)}$ reading an index as a tag bit and a point. For every string $x$, level $n$ and indices $i, j$,

$$ \mu_{\mathrm{tab}}(i, j) \;=\; \mu_{\mathrm{doubled}}\bigl(e_X(i),\ e_X(j)\bigr), \qquad \mu_{\mathrm{doubled}}((t, p), (t', q)) = \mu_{\mathcal{V}_n}(p, q) \text{ if } (t, t') = (\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}),\ \text{and } 0 \text{ otherwise}. $$

Per the docstring, the tabulated distribution is the sampler's on the block $(\mathrm{false}, \cdot) \times (\mathrm{true}, \cdot)$ and zero elsewhere, exactly the doubled game's: the distribution half of the match of the tabulation (obligation O2). It needs no boundedness hypothesis: per the module docstring, the sampler-side facts of the tabulation hold at every string and level, while the acceptance table needs $n$-boundedness.

**Formalization Note** The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.mu_clause`, with `G U x n` and `i j : Fin ((tab G U x n).nX + 1)` explicit and no hypothesis on `x` or `n`. `(tab G U x n).game` is `GameData.game`, the description read as a `MIPRE.Game`, with real-valued `μ` as above; `eXof G U x n` is an `Equiv` built from `tab_nX` and `Verifier.tagEquiv`; `doubledGame n T` is `(V.game n T).doubled`, with `μ p q = if p.1 = false ∧ q.1 = true then μ p.2 q.2 else 0`.

nodes.theorem_title: The tabulated acceptance table of the verifier a string denotes, read back on the doubled game
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ and a universal machine $U$. A bit string $x$ denotes the verifier $\mathcal V_x = \mathrm{Vof}(G, U, x)$: the compressed sampler $S^{\mathrm{compr}}_{\lambda_x}$ at the parameter $\lambda_x$ the string carries, and the string's decider datum $\mathcal D_x$, run by $U$ inside the question-length check, which together form its decider $\mathcal D_{\mathcal V_x}$. At level $n$ its questions are $\mathbb F_2^{s(n)}$, $s(n)$ the sampler's dimension, and its answers the strings of length at most $T = \mathrm{ansBound}(x, n) = \mathrm{bound}_G(n + \lambda_x)$. It is $n$-bounded (`IsBounded n`) when for all $m \ge 2$, $s(m) \le m^n$ and its sampler and decider run within cost $m^n(|d|+1)^n$ on every input $(m, d)$, and its description has size at most $n$.

$\mathrm{tab}(x, n)$ is a game description (`GameData`) of this game with doubled questions: question indices $0, \dots, n_X$, $n_X + 1 = 2^{s(n)+1}$, answer indices $0, \dots, n_A$, one per string of length at most $T$, and an acceptance list $\mathrm{acc}$ of tuples of naturals, with relabelings $e_X : \mathrm{Fin}(n_X + 1) \simeq \mathrm{Bool} \times \mathbb F_2^{s(n)}$ (a tag and a point) and $e_A : \mathrm{Fin}(n_A + 1) \simeq \{0,1\}^{\le T}$.

Assume $\mathcal V_x$ is $n$-bounded. For all question indices $i, j$ and answer indices $k, l$,

$$ (i, j, k, l) \in \mathrm{acc}(\mathrm{tab}(x, n)) \iff \mathrm{tag}(e_X i) = \mathsf{false} \wedge \mathrm{tag}(e_X j) = \mathsf{true} \wedge \mathcal D_{\mathcal V_x}\ \text{accepts}\ \bigl(n,\ \mathrm{bits}(\mathrm{pt}(e_X i)),\ \mathrm{bits}(\mathrm{pt}(e_X j)),\ e_A k,\ e_A l\bigr), $$

where a decider accepts an input when it halts on its encoding with output $1$ (`Decider.Accepts`), and $\mathrm{bits}$ lists the coordinates of a vector.

Acceptance clause of the tabulation obligation O2 of the halting reduction; with `mu_clause` it yields `tab_match`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.acc_mem_iff`. `tab G U x n` is `tabOf` on the encoded sampler and wrapped-decider programs of `Vof G U x`, the tabulated dimension, the cut `ansBound G x n` and `G.deg`; `acc` is the list `accListW`; `i j k l` are cast to `ℕ`; `(eXof … i).1`/`.2` are the tag and point and `(eAof … k).1` the string. The only hypothesis is `(Vof G U x).IsBounded n`; per the module docstring the match could not hold of every string, acceptance being $\Sigma_1$.

It reduces to four imported nodes: `MIPRE.Verifier.mem_accListW_iff` (membership in the tabulated acceptance list `accListW`), `MIPRE.Verifier.answerEquiv_symm_val` (the index of an answer in the enumeration of the strings of length at most $T$), `MIPRE.Cost.Machine.runs_of_runForD` (a result found by the budgeted run `runForD` is a genuine run) and `MIPRE.Cost.Eval.deterministic` (the ambient semantics is deterministic in result and cost). Eight helper lemmas are pasted from the source modules alongside it.

nodes.theorem_title: O2, the match: the doubled tabulation of the verifier a string denotes matches its doubled game
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ and a universal machine $U$. A bit string $x$ denotes the verifier $\mathcal V_x = \mathrm{Vof}(G, U, x)$: the compressed sampler $S^{\mathrm{compr}}_{\lambda_x}$ at the string's parameter $\lambda_x$ and the string's decider datum $\mathcal D_x$, run by $U$ inside the question-length check. At level $n$ its questions are $\mathbb F_2^{s(n)}$, $s(n)$ the sampler's dimension, and its answers the strings of length at most $T = \mathrm{ansBound}(x, n) = \mathrm{bound}_G(n + \lambda_x)$; it is $n$-bounded (`IsBounded n`) when for all $m \ge 2$, $s(m) \le m^n$ and its sampler and decider run within cost $m^n(|d|+1)^n$ on every input $(m, d)$, and its description has size at most $n$.

The doubled game $\mathcal V_x^{\mathrm{dbl}}(n, T)$ (`doubledGame`) is the synchronous game on $\mathrm{Bool} \times \mathbb F_2^{s(n)}$ with answers $\{0,1\}^{\le T}$: the pair $((\mathsf{false}, u), (\mathsf{true}, v))$ has the sampler's probability of $(u, v)$ and is accepted when the decider accepts $(n, \mathrm{bits}(u), \mathrm{bits}(v), a, b)$; every other pair has probability $0$ and is rejected. The description $\mathrm{tab}(x, n)$ (`GameData`) has indices $0, \dots, n_X$ and $0, \dots, n_A$; its game normalizes its weights and accepts the listed tuples except unequal answers to equal questions.

Assume $\mathcal V_x$ is $n$-bounded. Then there are bijections $e_X : \mathrm{Fin}(n_X + 1) \simeq \mathrm{Bool} \times \mathbb F_2^{s(n)}$ and $e_A : \mathrm{Fin}(n_A + 1) \simeq \{0,1\}^{\le T}$ such that, for all $i, j, k, l$,

$$ \mu_{\mathrm{tab}(x,n)}(i, j) = \mu^{\mathrm{dbl}}_{\mathcal V_x}(e_X i, e_X j),\quad D_{\mathrm{tab}(x,n)}(i, j, k, l) = D^{\mathrm{dbl}}_{\mathcal V_x}(e_X i, e_X j, e_A k, e_A l). $$

The match of obligation O2 of the halting reduction: it delivers the relabelings, not only the value, and needs no synchronicity of the decider, a description's forced rejections sitting on the diagonal, which the doubled distribution avoids; `tab_value` derives the value.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.tab_match`; the existential is over the two relabelings `eX`, `eA` with the types displayed above. `(tab G U x n).game` is `HaltingGameValue.GameData.game`, `doubledGame n T` is `((Vof G U x).game n T).doubled`; the clauses compare their fields `μ` and `D`. The only hypothesis is `IsBounded n`.

nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 20 lines and pastes no helper lemmas. It reduces to two imported nodes, one per clause: `MIPRE.Halting.mu_clause`, the distribution clause (the tabulated distribution is the sampler's on the block $(\mathsf{false}, \cdot) \times (\mathsf{true}, \cdot)$ and zero elsewhere), and `MIPRE.Halting.acc_mem_iff`, the acceptance clause (a tuple of indices is in the acceptance table exactly when the tags are Alice's and Bob's and the verifier's decider accepts). The witnesses of the existential are the relabelings `eXof G U x n` and `eAof G U x n` named in those nodes.

nodes.theorem_title: The canonicity walk accepts exactly the encodings of bit strings that are empty or end in a one
nodes.natural_language_statement:
In the ambient cost model, data are binary trees (`Data`, built from `nil` and `cons`), a bit is encoded as $\mathsf{false} \mapsto \mathtt{nil}$ and $\mathsf{true} \mapsto \mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{nil}, \mathtt{nil})$, and a bit string $l \in \{0,1\}^*$ as the $\mathtt{cons}$-chain of its encoded bits ending in $\mathtt{nil}$, written $\mathrm{encode}(l)$. The function $\mathrm{canonWalk} : \mathrm{Data} \to \mathrm{Bool} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ walks a datum while recording whether the string read so far is empty or ends in a one: $\mathrm{canonWalk}(\mathtt{nil}, b) = b$; $\mathrm{canonWalk}(\mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{nil}, r), b) = \mathrm{canonWalk}(r, \mathsf{false})$; $\mathrm{canonWalk}(\mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{nil},\mathtt{nil}), r), b) = \mathrm{canonWalk}(r, \mathsf{true})$; and $\mathrm{canonWalk}(\mathtt{cons}(h, r), b) = \mathsf{false}$ for any other head $h$.

For every datum $d$ and Boolean $b$,

$$ \mathrm{canonWalk}(d, b) = \mathsf{true} \iff \exists\, l \in \{0,1\}^*:\quad d = \mathrm{encode}(l)\ \wedge\ \bigl(l = \varepsilon \Rightarrow b = \mathsf{true}\bigr)\ \wedge\ \bigl(l \ne \varepsilon \Rightarrow \mathrm{last}(l) = 1\bigr). $$

This is the specification of the walk performed by the program `normBinProg`, with which the wrapper decider of the halting reduction normalizes the parameter of a description (a canonical binary numeral is a bit string that is empty or ends in a one). Its instance at $b = \mathsf{true}$ is `canonWalk_eq_isCanonBin`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Data.canonWalk_iff`. `BitStr` is `List Bool`, `encode l` is `Data.ofList Data.ofBool l`, and the last-bit condition is `l.getLast? = some true`; the empty and nonempty cases are stated as two separate implications, `(l = [] → b = true)` and `(l ≠ [] → l.getLast? = some true)`. For a datum that is not the encoding of any bit string, the right side is false because no `l` satisfies `d = encode l`. There are no hypotheses.

nodes.theorem_title: The canonicity walk started on true computes the canonical-binary-numeral test
nodes.natural_language_statement:
In the ambient cost model, natural numbers are encoded in binary, least significant bit first (Mathlib's `Nat.bits`), as bit strings, and bit strings as $\mathtt{cons}$-chains of encoded bits; so the encoding of a natural number is a bit string that is empty (the number $0$) or ends in a one. The test $\mathrm{isCanonBin} : \mathrm{Data} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ decodes a datum $d$ as a bit string: if it decodes to $l$, the result is the Boolean of $l = \varepsilon \vee \mathrm{last}(l) = 1$; if it does not decode, the result is $\mathsf{false}$. The walk $\mathrm{canonWalk}(d, b)$ (specified by `canonWalk_iff`) reads $d$ as a list of bits, failing on any non-bit element, and returns whether the string read is empty (in which case it returns the start value $b$) or ends in a one.

For every datum $d$,

$$ \mathrm{canonWalk}(d, \mathsf{true}) = \mathrm{isCanonBin}(d). $$

This identifies what the loop of the program `normBinProg` computes with the normalization test behind $\mathrm{normBin}(d) = \text{if } \mathrm{isCanonBin}(d) \text{ then } d \text{ else } \mathtt{nil}$, the total normalization of a parameter in which canonical binary numerals are kept and everything else reads as zero; `normBinProg_runs` uses it to state the program's output as $\mathrm{normBin}(d)$.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Data.canonWalk_eq_isCanonBin`, an equality of Booleans with no hypotheses. `isCanonBin` is a `match` on `decode d : Option BitStr`, with `decide (l = [] ∨ l.getLast? = some true)` in the `some l` branch and `false` in the `none` branch; `normBin` and `natOf d = ((decode (normBin d) : Option ℕ)).getD 0`, the parameter a datum denotes, are defined in `MIPRE/Foundations/Halting/Descriptions.lean`.

nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 23 lines and pastes no helper lemmas. It reduces to two imported nodes: `MIPRE.Cost.Data.canonWalk_iff`, the specification of the walk (it returns `true` exactly on the encodings of bit strings that are empty, when the start value is `true`, or end in a one), and `MIPRE.Cost.Data.encode_of_decode_bitStr` (if a datum decodes to the bit string `l`, then it equals `encode l`).

nodes.theorem_title: The canonicity loop computes the walk within cost linear in the list length times the state size
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Programs of the ambient cost model (`Prog`) use de Bruijn variables, and `Eval env p r t` is the timed big-step semantics: in the environment $\mathit{env}$ (a list of data, variable $0$ first) the program $p$ halts with result $r$ at cost $t$, one unit per evaluation rule plus the size of every value read. The construct $\mathtt{loop}(b)$ iterates $b$ on the state held in variable $0$: $b$ returns $\mathtt{cons}(\mathit{flag}, s')$, and the loop stops with result $s'$ if $\mathit{flag} = \mathtt{nil}$ and continues with state $s'$ otherwise (a body result $\mathtt{nil}$ stops with $\mathtt{nil}$). $\mathrm{canonBody}$ is the fixed program of the module that performs one step of the canonicity walk on a state $\mathtt{cons}(\mathit{rest}, \mathit{last})$. For a datum $d$, $\mathrm{size}(d)$ counts its nodes ($\mathtt{nil}$ counting one) and $\mathrm{spine}(d)$ is the length of its right spine, the length of $d$ read as a list; a Boolean is encoded as $\mathsf{false} \mapsto \mathtt{nil}$, $\mathsf{true} \mapsto \mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{nil}, \mathtt{nil})$.

Let $d$ be a datum, $\mathit{last}$ a Boolean, $\mathit{env}$ any environment and $S \in \mathbb N$ with $\mathrm{size}(d) + 3 \le S$. Then

$$ \exists\, t \le (\mathrm{spine}(d) + 1)\,(S + 21):\qquad \mathrm{Eval}\bigl(\mathtt{cons}(d, \mathrm{encode}(\mathit{last})) :: \mathit{env},\ \ \mathtt{loop}(\mathrm{canonBody}),\ \ \mathrm{encode}(\mathrm{canonWalk}(d, \mathit{last})),\ \ t\bigr). $$

The bound has the shape budget times size that the format checks of the wrapper decider need (`Decider.TimeBoundAt` charges $T \cdot (|\text{input}| + 1)$), the budget here being the number of list elements walked. It is the loop inside `normBinProg`, whose cost bound `normBinProg_runs` is assembled from it.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.canonLoop_runs`. The loop runs in the environment `Data.cons d (encode last) :: env` with an arbitrary tail `env`, and the result is `encode (canonWalk d last)`, the encoded Boolean of `Data.canonWalk`. The parameter `S` is any upper bound on `d.size + 3`, so that the cost can be bounded by a quantity fixed before the walk; the bound is `(d.spine + 1) * (S + 21)` with `Data.spine` the right-spine length, which the docstring writes as $(|d| + 1)(S + 21)$. The cost `t` is existentially quantified.

nodes.theorem_title: The normalization program computes normBin within an explicit quadratic cost bound
nodes.natural_language_statement:
In the ambient cost model, `Prog.Runs p x r t` means that the program $p$, run on the one-entry environment $[x]$, halts with result $r$ at cost $t$ (`Eval [x] p r t`). The total normalization of a parameter is $\mathrm{normBin}(d) = \text{if } \mathrm{isCanonBin}(d) \text{ then } d \text{ else } \mathtt{nil}$: a datum that is a canonical binary numeral (the encoding of a bit string that is empty or ends in a one, i.e. the binary encoding of a natural number) is kept, and everything else is sent to $\mathtt{nil}$, which denotes $0$. The program $\mathrm{normBinProg} = \mathtt{let}\ (\mathtt{let}\ \mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{var}\,0, \mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{nil},\mathtt{nil}))\ \mathtt{in}\ \mathtt{loop}(\mathrm{canonBody}))\ \mathtt{in}\ \mathtt{elim}\,0\ \mathtt{nil}\ (\mathtt{var}\,3)$ builds the state $(d, \mathsf{true})$, runs the canonicity loop on it, and returns $\mathtt{nil}$ if the loop returned $\mathtt{nil}$ and the input $d$ otherwise. For a datum $d$, $\mathrm{size}(d)$ is its number of nodes and $\mathrm{spine}(d)$ its length as a list.

For every datum $d$,

$$ \exists\, t \le (\mathrm{spine}(d) + 2)\,(\mathrm{size}(d) + 25) + 3\,\mathrm{size}(d) + 10:\qquad \mathrm{normBinProg}\ \text{on the input}\ d\ \text{halts with}\ \mathrm{normBin}(d)\ \text{at cost}\ t. $$

This is the correctness and cost statement of the third of the format-check programs of the wrapper decider of the halting reduction (after the bit-walk and the equality test): the parameter of a description is normalized so that every string names a parameter. The cost is quadratic in the size of the input, as for the other walks, which copy the remainder of the list at each step.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.normBinProg_runs`, with no hypotheses; the result is `normBin d` (`Data.normBin`) and the cost `t` is existential with the bound `(d.spine + 2) * (d.size + 25) + 3 * d.size + 10`, in which `Data.spine` (list length) and `Data.size` (node count) are distinct measures that the docstring both writes as $|d|$.
nodes.source: https://github.com/vidick/MIPRE-formalization/blob/70cbf1c52e3d5e1dff1162fdf952c9a9f4bd99ed/MIPRE/Foundations/Halting/Lists.lean#L586-L608; the parameter normalization of the wrapper decider of blueprint rem:compression-abstract, item 1, per the module docstring; no blueprint label is attached to this declaration
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 19 lines and pastes no helper lemmas. It reduces to two imported nodes: `MIPRE.Cost.Prog.canonLoop_runs`, the run and cost bound of the canonicity loop on the state `cons d (encode last)`, and `MIPRE.Cost.Data.canonWalk_eq_isCanonBin`, which identifies the loop's output `canonWalk d true` with the normalization test `isCanonBin d` that defines `normBin`.

nodes.theorem_title: A power-of-two cutoff in the encoded size of the parameter dominates the compressor's answer bound at the fixed level
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $G$ be a gap-preserving compression instance (`GapCompression`). Its polynomial $\mathrm{bound}_G \in \mathbb N[X]$ is the paper's $\mathrm{poly}(n, \lambda)$: evaluated at $n + \lambda$ it bounds the running times of the compressed verifier at index $n$ with parameter $\lambda$, the dimension of the compressed sampler, and the length of the answers the compressed decider can accept. $C_G = \max(C_0, 2)$ is the fixed level at which the paper-route halting reduction plays its game, $C_0$ the constant of the compression theorem. For a natural number $\lambda$, $|\lambda| = \mathrm{esize}(\lambda)$ denotes the size of its encoding in the ambient model, the number of nodes of the binary (least significant bit first) encoding of $\lambda$, which lies between $2\ell + 1$ and $4\ell + 1$ for $\ell$ the binary length of $\lambda$.

$$ \exists\, K \in \mathbb N\ \ \forall\, \lambda \in \mathbb N:\qquad \mathrm{bound}_G(C_G + \lambda) \ \le\ 2^{\,K + \deg(\mathrm{bound}_G) \cdot |\lambda|}. $$

The class decider of the polynomial-time halting reduction cuts the answers at $2^{K + \deg \cdot |\lambda(z)|}$, a power of two so that it can be computed from $|\lambda(z)|$ in unary and is polynomial in $\lambda(z)$; this lemma provides the constant $K$ for which the cutoff is at least the compressor's answer bound at level $C_G$, which is the hypothesis `hK` of `classV_values` and is discharged with it in `re_subset_mipstar_of`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.exists_cut_ge`; of the section variables only `G` occurs in it. `G.bound.natDegree` is Mathlib's degree of a polynomial over `ℕ`, `G.bound.eval` its evaluation, `esize lam` is `(encode lam).size` for the binary encoding of `ℕ`, and `C G` is `max G.C₀ 2`. The constant `K` is existentially quantified and the statement does not make it explicit.

nodes.theorem_title: The class verifier of the polynomial-time halting reduction is efficient on every input
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs. The class verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}} = \mathrm{classV}(G, U, U_T, \Lambda_0, K, R)$ is a polynomial-time verifier (`PolyVerifier`): the closed sampler program $\mathrm{sampProg}$, which on $(z, r)$ outputs the question pair of the halting verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$, $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|R(z)|$, at the fixed level $C_G$ on the seed's first $s(C_G)$ bits; the closed decider program $\mathrm{decProg}$, which rejects answers longer than the cutoff $\mathrm{cut}(z) = 2^{K + \deg(\mathrm{bound}_G)\cdot|\lambda(z)|}$ and otherwise runs the decider of $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z),\lambda(z)}$ on $(C_G, x, y, a, b)$ through $U$; and the polynomial $P = \mathrm{classP}$ chosen above the module's four cost bounds. Write $B(z) = P(|z|)$.

$\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is efficient on $z$ (`Efficient z`) when (i) for every seed $r$ of length $B(z)$ there are strings $x, y$ of length at most $B(z)$ and a cost $t \le P(|z| + |r|)$ such that $\mathrm{sampProg}$ on $\mathrm{encode}(z, r)$ halts with $\mathrm{encode}(x, y)$ at cost $t$; (ii) for all $x, y, a, b$, $\mathrm{decProg}$ halts on $\mathrm{encode}(z, x, y, a, b)$ within cost $P(|z| + |x| + |y| + |a| + |b|)$; (iii) if one of $x, y, a, b$ is longer than $B(z)$, the decider does not accept $(z, x, y, a, b)$. The theorem states

$$ \forall\, z \in \{0,1\}^*:\qquad \mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}}\ \text{is efficient on}\ z,\ \text{i.e. (i), (ii), (iii) hold for } z. $$

Efficiency on every input is the first requirement of membership in $\mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$ (`MIPStar`), which `re_subset_mipstar_of` takes from this theorem.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.classV_efficient`, with `G U UT Λ₀ K R` as section variables. `PolyVerifier.Efficient` is a structure with the fields `sampler_runs`, `decider_time` (a `HaltsWithin`) and `rejects_long`, acceptance being `∃ t, decider.Runs (encode (z, x, y, a, b)) (encode true) t`. `classP` is the sum of the polynomials of the `PolyBounded` witnesses for `sampB`, `dimB`, `decB`, `cutB`, so the bounds are polynomial but not in closed form; all are in the total input length.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 15 lines. It reduces to three imported nodes, one per clause of efficiency: `MIPRE.Halting.sampProg_runs` (the sampler halts with the question pair within `sampB (|z| + |r|)` on any seed at least `dimz z` long), `MIPRE.Halting.decProg_runs` (the decider halts on every input within `decB` of the total input length) and `MIPRE.Halting.decProg_accepts` (acceptance means both answers are within the cutoff and the halting verifier's decider accepts at the fixed level). Seven helper lemmas are pasted from the source modules alongside it.

nodes.theorem_title: Seeds of the class verifier producing a given question pair: a count over $\mathbb F_2^{s(C)}$ times $2^{B(z) - s(C)}$
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs, and let $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}} = \mathrm{classV}(G, U, U_T, \Lambda_0, K, R)$ be the class verifier with bound $B(z)$. On an input $z$ it plays the halting verifier $\mathcal W_z = \mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$, $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|R(z)|$, whose sampler is the compressed sampler $S^{\mathrm{compr}}_{\lambda(z)}$; at the fixed level $C_G$ this sampler has dimension $s = s(C_G)$ and two conditionally linear functions $L^{\mathsf A}, L^{\mathsf B} : \mathbb F_2^{s} \to \mathbb F_2^{s}$, one per player. The questions of $\mathcal W_z$ at level $C_G$ are the vectors of $\mathbb F_2^{s}$, and $\iota$ (`qEmb`) embeds them into the strings of length at most $B(z)$ by listing their coordinates. The seed count $\mathrm{seedCount}_z(x', y')$ is the number of seeds $r \in \{0,1\}^{B(z)}$ for which the sampler's output on $\mathrm{encode}(z, r)$, read as a pair of strings of length at most $B(z)$, is $(x', y')$.

For all $x, y \in \mathbb F_2^{s}$,

$$ \mathrm{seedCount}_z(\iota x, \iota y) \;=\; \#\bigl\{ v \in \mathbb F_2^{s} :\ L^{\mathsf A}(v) = x \ \wedge\ L^{\mathsf B}(v) = y \bigr\} \cdot 2^{\,B(z) - s}. $$

The seed count is the numerator of the question distribution of the game $G_z$ of the class verifier, $\mu_{G_z}(x', y') = \mathrm{seedCount}_z(x', y') / 2^{B(z)}$; dividing, `classV_game_mu` identifies $\mu_{G_z}$ on the embedded questions with the compressed sampler's distribution.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.seedCount_eq`, with `G U UT Λ₀ K R` as section variables. `(Vz G U UT Λ₀ R z).Questions (C G)` is `Fin (dimz G Λ₀ R z) → ZMod 2`, the count is `(Finset.univ.filter …).card` over it, and the two conditions are `((Vz …).sampler.cl (C G) .alice).eval v = x` and the same for `.bob`. `qEmb G U UT Λ₀ K R z` is an embedding into `Answers ((classV …).B z)` with `(qEmb … v).1 = CL.toBits v`, and `seedCount` is `PolyVerifier.seedCount`, the length of a filtered enumeration `Data.bitStrsOfLen (B z)`. The exponent `(classV …).B z - dimz G Λ₀ R z` is natural-number subtraction; the module proves `dimz_le_B`, so it is not truncated.

nodes.theorem_title: The question distribution of the class verifier's game is the compressed sampler's on the embedded questions
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs; let $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}} = \mathrm{classV}(G, U, U_T, \Lambda_0, K, R)$ be the class verifier with bound $B(z)$, and $\mathcal W_z = \mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$ the halting verifier it plays on $z$, with $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|R(z)|$. The game $G_z$ of $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}}$ on $z$ (`PolyVerifier.game`) has as questions and answers the strings of length at most $B(z)$; its question distribution is $\mu_{G_z}(x', y') = \mathrm{seedCount}_z(x', y') / 2^{B(z)}$, the pushforward of the uniform seed of length $B(z)$ through the sampler, and its decision predicate is the decider's acceptance. The game of $\mathcal W_z$ at level $C_G$ with answers of length at most $T$ (`Verifier.game`) has questions $\mathbb F_2^{s}$, $s = s(C_G)$ the compressed sampler's dimension, and the distribution of the sampler: the law of $(L^{\mathsf A}(v), L^{\mathsf B}(v))$ for $v$ uniform in $\mathbb F_2^{s}$. $\iota$ (`qEmb`) embeds $\mathbb F_2^{s}$ into the strings of length at most $B(z)$ by listing coordinates, and $\mathrm{cut}(z) = 2^{K + \deg(\mathrm{bound}_G) \cdot |\lambda(z)|}$ is the class decider's answer cutoff.

For all $x, y \in \mathbb F_2^{s}$,

$$ \mu_{G_z}(\iota x, \iota y) \;=\; \mu_{\mathcal W_z,\, C_G,\, \mathrm{cut}(z)}(x, y). $$

Together with `classV_game_support`, which says that $\mu_{G_z}$ vanishes off the image of $\iota$, this makes $G_z$ a relabeling of the game of $\mathcal W_z$ at the fixed level on the question side; `classV_value` uses both to transfer the quantum value.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is uploaded as `MIPRE.Halting.classV_game_mu`; in the source at the pinned commit it is `MIPRE.Halting.classV_game_μ`. The right-hand game is `(Vz G U UT Λ₀ R z).game (C G) (cutz G Λ₀ K R z)`; its answer cut appears only in its type, since `Verifier.game n T` has `μ := V.sampler.dist n`, which unfolds to `CL.clDist` of the two CL functions, a count divided by `Fintype.card (Fin s → ZMod 2)`. The left side is `PolyVerifier.game_μ`, a quotient of `seedCount` by `2 ^ B z` in `ℝ`.

nodes.theorem_title: The class verifier's question distribution is supported on the embedded questions of the compressed sampler
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs, and let $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}} = \mathrm{classV}(G, U, U_T, \Lambda_0, K, R)$ be the class verifier, with bound $B(z)$ and game $G_z$ on the input $z$: a game whose questions and answers are the strings of length at most $B(z)$, with question distribution $\mu_{G_z}(x', y') = \mathrm{seedCount}_z(x', y')/2^{B(z)}$, the number of seeds of length $B(z)$ on which the sampler outputs $(x', y')$, normalized. On $z$ the class verifier plays the halting verifier $\mathcal W_z = \mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$, $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|R(z)|$, whose questions at the fixed level $C_G$ are the vectors of $\mathbb F_2^{s}$, $s = s(C_G)$ the compressed sampler's dimension; $\iota$ (`qEmb`) embeds them into the strings of length at most $B(z)$ by listing their coordinates.

For all strings $x', y'$ of length at most $B(z)$,

$$ \mu_{G_z}(x', y') \ne 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \bigl(\exists\, x \in \mathbb F_2^{s}:\ \iota x = x'\bigr)\ \wedge\ \bigl(\exists\, y \in \mathbb F_2^{s}:\ \iota y = y'\bigr). $$

This is the support hypothesis under which a game may be restricted to the image of an embedding of its question alphabets without changing its quantum value (`quantumValue_restrictQuestions`, named in the module docstring); with `classV_game_mu` it reduces the game of the class verifier to the game of $\mathcal W_z$ at the fixed level in `classV_value`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.classV_game_support`, with `G U UT Λ₀ K R` as section variables. `x' y'` have type `Answers ((classV G U UT Λ₀ K R).B z)`, that is `{a : BitStr // a.length ≤ B z}`; the hypothesis `h` is `((classV …).game z).μ x' y' ≠ 0` in `ℝ`; the two existentials range over `(Vz G U UT Λ₀ R z).Questions (C G)`, which is `Fin (dimz G Λ₀ R z) → ZMod 2`, and `qEmb G U UT Λ₀ K R z` is the embedding `v ↦ ⟨CL.toBits v, _⟩`.

nodes.theorem_title: The quantum value of the class verifier's game equals that of the halting verifier at the fixed level with answers cut
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs. The class verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}} = \mathrm{classV}(G, U, U_T, \Lambda_0, K, R)$ is a polynomial-time verifier whose game $G_z$ on the input $z$ has as questions and answers the strings of length at most $B(z)$, the question pair being the sampler's output on a uniform seed of length $B(z)$ and the decision the decider's acceptance. On $z$ it plays the halting verifier $\mathcal W_z = \mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$, $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|R(z)|$, at the fixed level $C_G = \max(C_0, 2)$, with the answers cut at $\mathrm{cut}(z) = 2^{K + \deg(\mathrm{bound}_G)\cdot|\lambda(z)|}$. The quantum value $\mathrm{val}^*$ of a game is the supremum, over all tensor-product strategies (a shared state and a projective measurement for each player and question), of the probability of acceptance; for a verifier, $\mathrm{val}^*(\mathcal W, n, T)$ is the quantum value of its game at index $n$ with answers of length at most $T$.

For every input $z$,

$$ \mathrm{val}^*(G_z) \;=\; \mathrm{val}^*\bigl(\mathcal W_z,\ C_G,\ \mathrm{cut}(z)\bigr). $$

This transfers the value of the game of the polynomial-time class verifier to that of the halting verifier at the fixed level, where blueprint `thm:halting` in the paper's form (`halting_paper`) gives value $1$ when $R(z)$ halts and at most $1/2$ when it does not; `classV_values` draws that consequence. The module docstring describes $G_z$ as the restriction of $\mathcal W_z$'s game to the questions of length $s(C_G)$, with the answers extended by always-rejected ones.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.classV_value`, with `G U UT Λ₀ K R` as section variables. The left side is `quantumValue ((classV G U UT Λ₀ K R).game z)`, `MIPRE.quantumValue` of a `Game` on four copies of `Answers (B z)`, a supremum in `ℝ` over `TensorProductStrategy`; the right side is `(Vz G U UT Λ₀ R z).valStar (C G) (cutz G Λ₀ K R z)`, which unfolds to `quantumValue ((Vz …).game (C G) (cutz …))`, with `Vz` an abbreviation for `Vpaper G U UT (R z) (lamz Λ₀ R z)`. There are no hypotheses on `z`, `Λ₀` or `K`.

Five helper lemmas are pasted from the source modules alongside it.

nodes.theorem_title: The class verifier's game has value 1 when $R(z)$ halts and value at most 1/2 when it does not
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, a natural number $K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs. Let $\Lambda_0 = \mathrm{lamThreshold}(G, U, U_T)$ be the threshold of blueprint `lem:lambda` for the search program $\mathrm{semL}$ of the halting verifier: for $\lambda \ge \Lambda_0 + 4|M|$ the halting verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{M, \lambda}$ is $\lambda$-bounded. Let $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{cl}} = \mathrm{classV}(G, U, U_T, \Lambda_0, K, R)$ be the class verifier at this threshold and $G_z$ its game on the input $z$, whose quantum value $\mathrm{val}^*(G_z)$ is the supremum of the acceptance probability over tensor-product strategies. A program $p$ halts on the empty input when it halts on the datum $\mathtt{nil}$ (`Halts p nil`). Assume the cutoff dominates the compressor's bound at the fixed level $C_G$:

$\mathrm{bound}_G(C_G + \lambda) \le 2^{K + \deg(\mathrm{bound}_G)\cdot|\lambda|}$ for every $\lambda \in \mathbb N$ (hypothesis `hK`, supplied by `exists_cut_ge`).

Then, for every input $z$,

$$ \bigl(R(z)\ \text{halts on}\ \mathtt{nil} \ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{val}^*(G_z) = 1\bigr)\ \ \wedge\ \ \bigl(R(z)\ \text{does not halt on}\ \mathtt{nil} \ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{val}^*(G_z) \le \tfrac12\bigr). $$

These are the completeness and soundness clauses of membership in $\mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$ for a language that $R$ reduces to halting on the empty input: blueprint `thm:halting` at the fixed level, transported from the halting verifier to the polynomial-time class verifier; `re_subset_mipstar_of` combines them with `classV_efficient`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.classV_values`. The parameter slot of `classV` is instantiated with `lamThreshold G U UT`, not with the section variable `Λ₀`, and `K` is constrained only by `hK : ∀ lam, G.bound.eval (C G + lam) ≤ 2 ^ (K + G.bound.natDegree * esize lam)`, with `esize lam` the size of the binary encoding of `lam`. `Halts (R z) .nil` is `∃ r t, Eval [.nil] (R z) r t`, `quantumValue` is `MIPRE.quantumValue` of `(classV …).game z` in `ℝ`, and `1 / 2` is a real number.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 13 lines. It reduces to four imported nodes: `MIPRE.Halting.classV_value` (the value of the class verifier's game is that of the halting verifier at the fixed level with answers cut at `cutz z`), `MIPRE.Halting.hasPerfectPCC_of_halts` and `MIPRE.Halting.valStar_le_of_not_halts` (the two branches of blueprint thm:halting for the halting verifier at level `C`: a value-1 PCC strategy when `M` halts, value at most `1/2` when it does not), and `MIPRE.Halting.accepts_iff` (the acceptance characterization of the halting verifier's decider, blueprint lem:dhalt-values). Fourteen helper lemmas are pasted from the source modules alongside it.

nodes.theorem_title: $\mathrm{RE} \subseteq \mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$, given a gap-preserving compressor and the two universal machines
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`: the data and guarantees of blueprint `thm:compression`), an efficient universal machine $U$ (`UniversalMachine`) and a clocked universal machine $U_T$ (`ClockedUniversalMachine`) of the ambient cost model. A language $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ is recursively enumerable (`IsRE L`) when membership in $L$ is the domain of a partial computable function (Mathlib's `REPred`). It is in $\mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$ (`MIPStar L`, the paper's `def:mipstar`) when there is a polynomial-time verifier $\mathcal V$ (`PolyVerifier`: a closed sampler program, a closed decider program and one polynomial time bound) that is efficient on every input $z$ (its sampler, on every seed of length $B(z)$, halts within the polynomial with a pair of strings of length at most $B(z)$; its decider halts within the polynomial on every input and rejects whenever one of the four strings is longer than $B(z)$), and whose game $G_z$ on $z$ (questions and answers the strings of length at most $B(z)$, the question pair the sampler's output on a uniform seed, the decision the decider's) has quantum value $\mathrm{val}^*(G_z) = 1$ when $z \in L$ and $\mathrm{val}^*(G_z) \le 1/2$ when $z \notin L$.

$$ \forall\, L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*:\qquad L \in \mathrm{RE} \ \Longrightarrow\ L \in \mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1). $$

This is the inclusion $\mathrm{RE} \subseteq \mathrm{MIP}^*$ of blueprint `thm:mipstar-eq-re` for the paper's class, in the form that is conditional on an instance of gap-preserving compression and on the two universal machines, which enter as explicit hypotheses. The module docstring places the unconditional forms in `MIPRE/Background/Pipeline.lean` and `MIPRE/MainTheorem.lean`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.re_subset_mipstar_of`, with `G U UT` as explicit arguments (brought into the statement by `include G U UT`) and `L : Set BitStr` implicit. `IsRE L` is `REPred (· ∈ L)` on `BitStr = List Bool`, and `MIPStar L` is `∃ V : PolyVerifier, (∀ z, V.Efficient z) ∧ ∀ z, (z ∈ L → quantumValue (V.game z) = 1) ∧ (z ∉ L → quantumValue (V.game z) ≤ 1 / 2)`. In the formalization's reading of `def:mipstar` the time bounds of the sampler and the decider are polynomials in the total input length, and the rejection of overlong messages is a separate clause of `Efficient`, which is what makes `G_z` a finite game on the strings of length at most `B z`.

Four helper lemmas are pasted from the source modules alongside it.

nodes.theorem_title: $\mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1) = \mathrm{RE}$ for the paper's class, given a gap-preserving compressor and the two universal machines
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$ (`GapCompression`: the data and guarantees of blueprint `thm:compression`), an efficient universal machine $U$ and a clocked universal machine $U_T$ of the ambient cost model. For a language $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$, $\mathrm{IsRE}(L)$ says that membership in $L$ is the domain of a partial computable function (Mathlib's `REPred`), and $\mathrm{MIPStar}(L)$, the paper's $\mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$ of `def:mipstar`, says that some polynomial-time verifier (a closed sampler program, a closed decider program and one polynomial time bound) is efficient on every input and has a game of quantum value $1$ on the members of $L$ and of quantum value at most $1/2$ off them; the game on $z$ has as questions and answers the strings of length at most the polynomial at $|z|$, its question pair is the sampler's output on a uniform seed, and its decision is the decider's acceptance.

$$ \mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1) \;=\; \mathrm{RE}, $$

an equality of the two predicates on languages: for every $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$, $L \in \mathrm{MIP}^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$ if and only if $L \in \mathrm{RE}$.

This is blueprint `thm:mipstar-eq-re` for the paper's class, in the form conditional on an instance of gap-preserving compression and on the two universal machines, which are explicit hypotheses. It combines the two inclusions: $\mathrm{RE} \subseteq \mathrm{MIP}^*$ (`re_subset_mipstar_of`, from the polynomial-time halting reduction) and $\mathrm{MIP}^* \subseteq \mathrm{RE}$ (the inclusion of the paper's class in the computable class by tabulation, and of that in $\mathrm{RE}$ by the lower approximation of the quantum value). The module docstring places the unconditional forms in `MIPRE/Background/Pipeline.lean` and `MIPRE/MainTheorem.lean`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.mipstar_eq_re_of : MIPStar = IsRE`, an equality of two functions `Set BitStr → Prop`, so that it is the pointwise equivalence up to function and propositional extensionality; `G U UT` are explicit arguments brought in by `include G U UT`. `IsRE L` is `REPred (· ∈ L)` and `MIPStar L` is `∃ V : PolyVerifier, (∀ z, V.Efficient z) ∧ ∀ z, (z ∈ L → quantumValue (V.game z) = 1) ∧ (z ∉ L → quantumValue (V.game z) ≤ 1 / 2)`, with the time bounds in the total input length and the rejection of overlong messages as a separate clause of `Efficient`. The docstring cites blueprint `thm:mipstar-eq-re` for the paper's class.

nodes.theorem_title: The class verifier's sampler halts with the halting verifier's question pair within the explicit cost bound
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a natural number $\Lambda_0$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs. For an input $z$ write $M = R(z)$, $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|M|$ ($|M|$ the size of the encoding of $M$), $S_z = S^{\mathrm{compr}}_{\lambda(z)}$ for the compressed sampler at this parameter, $s = s(C_G)$ for its dimension at the fixed level $C_G = \max(C_0, 2)$, and $L^{\mathsf A}, L^{\mathsf B} : \mathbb F_2^{s} \to \mathbb F_2^{s}$ for its two conditionally linear functions at that level. The question of player $w$ on the seed $r$ is $q_w(z, r) = \mathrm{bits}\bigl(L^{w}(\mathrm{vec}_s(r_{< s}))\bigr)$: the vector of $\mathbb F_2^{s}$ read off the first $s$ bits of $r$ (missing bits read as $0$), mapped by $L^{w}$, listed as a bit string. The sampler $\mathrm{sampProg}$ of the class verifier computes $M$, $\lambda(z)$ and the program of $S_z$, asks $S_z$ its dimension through $U$, converts it to unary, and asks Alice's and then Bob's marginal at the first $s$ bits of the seed through $U$. $\mathrm{sampB}(m)$ is the module's explicit cost expression in the total input length $m$, assembled from the time polynomials of the three stage functions, the overhead polynomial of $U$, $\mathrm{bound}_G$ and the time polynomial of $R$, and polynomially bounded (`polyBounded_sampB`).

Let $z, r$ be bit strings with $s \le |r|$. Then

$$ \exists\, t \le \mathrm{sampB}(|z| + |r|):\qquad \mathrm{sampProg}\ \text{on the input}\ \mathrm{encode}(z, r)\ \text{halts with}\ \mathrm{encode}\bigl(q_{\mathsf A}(z, r),\ q_{\mathsf B}(z, r)\bigr)\ \text{at cost}\ t. $$

This is the sampler clause of the efficiency of the class verifier (`classV_efficient`) and the determination of its question pair on every seed, from which the uniform seed of length $B(z) \ge s$ pushes forward to the compressed sampler's distribution (`seedCount_eq`, `classV_game_mu`).

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.sampProg_runs`, with `G U Λ₀ R` the section variables occurring in it. `Prog.Runs p x r t` is `Eval [x] p r t`; `qOf G Λ₀ R w z r` is `CL.toBits (((Sz G Λ₀ R z).cl (C G) w).eval (CL.ofBits (dimz G Λ₀ R z) (r.take (dimz G Λ₀ R z))))`; the hypothesis `hd : dimz G Λ₀ R z ≤ r.length` asks only that the seed be long enough, and the bound `sampB G U Λ₀ R (z.length + r.length)` is in the total input length, as `PolyVerifier.Efficient.sampler_runs` requires. The cost `t` is existential.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 162 lines, the longest of this packet. It reduces to one imported node, `MIPRE.Cost.Eval.deterministic` (the ambient semantics is deterministic in result and cost), and nine helper lemmas are pasted from the source modules alongside it. The module docstring describes the program whose run it bounds as three stages joined by calls of the universal machine (`A1`: the machine, the parameter and the compressed sampler's program; the dimension query; the conversion to unary; `A2`: Alice's marginal on the first `s` bits of the seed; `A3`: Bob's), and the bound `sampB` as the sum of the corresponding stage costs.

nodes.theorem_title: The preparation step of the class decider: cutoff check, then the halting verifier's decider on the input at level $C$
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs. The decider of the class verifier runs a polynomial-time preparation $D_1$ and then the universal machine on its output. $D_1$ (`PolyTimeFun`: a function together with a closed program computing it on encodings and a polynomial time bound) takes the decider's input $(z, x, y, a, b)$, five bit strings, to a pair of a program and a datum: the program to run and its input. Write $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|R(z)|$, $\mathrm{cut}(z) = 2^{K + \deg(\mathrm{bound}_G)\cdot|\lambda(z)|}$ for the answer cutoff, $\mathrm{wdec}(z)$ for the program of the decider of the halting verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$ (its decider $\mathrm{dec}(R(z), \lambda(z))$ wrapped in the question-length check), $C_G = \max(C_0, 2)$ for the fixed level, and $\mathrm{falseProg}$ for the program that halts with output $\mathsf{false}$ on every input.

For all bit strings $z, x, y, a, b$,

$$ D_1(z, x, y, a, b) = \begin{cases} \bigl(\mathrm{wdec}(z),\ \mathrm{encode}(C_G, x, y, a, b)\bigr) & \text{if } |a| \le \mathrm{cut}(z) \text{ and } |b| \le \mathrm{cut}(z), \\ (\mathrm{falseProg},\ \mathtt{nil}) & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} $$

This is the computation rule of the preparation, from which the acceptance characterization `decProg_accepts` and the cost bound `decProg_runs` of the class decider are stated: the decider rejects an answer longer than the cutoff outright, and otherwise defers to the halting verifier's decider on the input at the fixed level.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.D1_apply`, with `G U UT Λ₀ K R` as section variables; `D1 G U UT Λ₀ K R` is built from the combinators `PolyTimeFun.ite`, `leNat`, `lenBin`, `pair` and the pieces `cutzF`, `wF`, `inputF`, `rejF`, and is applied to the quintuple through its coercion to a function. The right side is two nested `if … then … else` on `a.length ≤ cutz G Λ₀ K R z` and then `b.length ≤ cutz G Λ₀ K R z`, both failing branches being `(falseProg, Data.nil)`; `wdec G U UT Λ₀ R z` is `(Vpaper G U UT (R z) (lamz Λ₀ R z)).decider.prog`, and `falseProg` is `Prog.const (encode false)`.

The theorem is the computation rule on which `decProg_accepts` and `decProg_runs` rest.

nodes.theorem_title: Acceptance of the class decider: both answers within the cutoff and the halting verifier's decider accepts at level $C$
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs. The class decider $\mathrm{decProg}$ runs the preparation $D_1$ on its input $(z, x, y, a, b)$ and then the universal machine $U$ on the pair of a program and an input that $D_1$ returns: the constant-$\mathsf{false}$ program if $a$ or $b$ is longer than the cutoff $\mathrm{cut}(z) = 2^{K + \deg(\mathrm{bound}_G)\cdot|\lambda(z)|}$, $\lambda(z) = \Lambda_0 + 4|R(z)|$, and otherwise the decider of the halting verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$ on $(C_G, x, y, a, b)$, $C_G = \max(C_0, 2)$ the fixed level. A decider accepts an input when it halts on its encoding with output $\mathsf{true}$ (`Decider.Accepts`); the decider of $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{M, \lambda}$ is the decider $\mathrm{dec}(M, \lambda)$ wrapped in the question-length check, so its acceptance includes that $x$ and $y$ have the compressed sampler's dimension.

For all bit strings $z, x, y, a, b$,

$$ \bigl(\exists\, t:\ \mathrm{decProg}\ \text{on}\ \mathrm{encode}(z, x, y, a, b)\ \text{halts with}\ \mathrm{encode}(\mathsf{true})\ \text{at cost}\ t\bigr) \iff |a| \le \mathrm{cut}(z)\ \wedge\ |b| \le \mathrm{cut}(z)\ \wedge\ \mathcal D^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}\ \text{accepts}\ (C_G, x, y, a, b). $$

The left side is the decision predicate of the class verifier's game on $z$. The equivalence identifies it with the halting verifier's at the fixed level, under the cutoff: it gives the rejection of overlong answers in `classV_efficient` and the transfer of the decision predicate in `classV_value`.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.decProg_accepts`, with `G U UT Λ₀ K R` as section variables. The left side is `∃ t, (decProg G U UT Λ₀ K R).Runs (encode (z, x, y, a, b)) (encode true) t`, which is `PolyVerifier.Accepts` of `classV` unfolded; the third conjunct on the right is `(Vpaper G U UT (R z) (lamz Λ₀ R z)).decider.Accepts (C G) x y a b`, the acceptance of the wrapped decider. `decProg` is `seq (D1 …).code U.univ`. The equivalence is between propositions; no hypothesis is placed on the five strings.

It reduces to two imported nodes: `MIPRE.Halting.D1_apply` (the computation rule of the preparation: the wrapped decider of the halting verifier with the input `(C, x, y, a, b)` when both answers are within the cutoff, the constant-false program on `nil` otherwise) and `MIPRE.Cost.Eval.deterministic` (the ambient semantics is deterministic in result and cost). One helper lemma is pasted from the source modules alongside it.

nodes.theorem_title: The class decider halts on every input within the explicit cost bound in the total input length
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression instance $G$, a universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $U_T$, naturals $\Lambda_0, K$ and a polynomial-time map $R$ from bit strings to programs. The class decider $\mathrm{decProg}$ runs the preparation $D_1$ on its input $(z, x, y, a, b)$ (five bit strings) and then the universal machine $U$ on the program and input that $D_1$ returns: the constant-$\mathsf{false}$ program if $a$ or $b$ exceeds the cutoff $\mathrm{cut}(z)$, and otherwise the wrapped decider of the halting verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}_{R(z), \lambda(z)}$ on $(C_G, x, y, a, b)$. The cost bound $\mathrm{decB}(m)$ is the module's explicit expression in the total input length $m$: $3\,\mathrm{TDB}(m) + \mathrm{bound}_U\bigl(\mathrm{TDB}(m) + \mathrm{WZ}(\mathrm{zB}(m)) + \mathrm{constCost}\bigr) + 6$, where $\mathrm{TDB}(m)$ is the time polynomial of $D_1$ at $4m + 9$, $\mathrm{bound}_U$ the overhead polynomial of $U$, $\mathrm{WZ}$ the cost bound of the wrapped decider of the halting verifier from `Paper/Cost.lean`, evaluated at a common bound $\mathrm{zB}(m)$ on the sizes it depends on; it is polynomially bounded (`polyBounded_decB`).

For all bit strings $z, x, y, a, b$,

$$ \exists\, r\ \ \exists\, t \le \mathrm{decB}(|z| + |x| + |y| + |a| + |b|):\qquad \mathrm{decProg}\ \text{on the input}\ \mathrm{encode}(z, x, y, a, b)\ \text{halts with}\ r\ \text{at cost}\ t. $$

This is the decider's time clause of the efficiency of the class verifier (`classV_efficient`): the decider is total, and its cost is polynomial in the total input length, which is how the formalization reads the paper's requirement that the decider run in time $\mathrm{poly}(|z|)$ even on long inputs, since a program of the ambient model reads a string only by walking it.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Halting.decProg_runs`, with `G U UT Λ₀ K R` as section variables. The output `r` is unconstrained (the theorem is a `HaltsWithin` statement written out), the cost `t` is existential with the bound `decB G U UT Λ₀ K R (z.length + x.length + y.length + a.length + b.length)`, and `decB` is a `noncomputable def` of `ClassVerifier.lean` in terms of `TDB`, `U.bound`, `WZ`, `zB` and `constCost`.
nodes.explanation: The uploaded proof is 59 lines. It reduces to one imported node, `MIPRE.Halting.D1_apply` (the computation rule of the preparation, which fixes the program and input that the universal machine then runs in each of the two cases), and one helper lemma is pasted from the source modules alongside it. The bound `decB` it establishes is the one above which `Paper/ClassMain.lean` chooses the class verifier's polynomial.

nodes.theorem_title: Counting, in a list of bit strings each extended by a leading bit, those that satisfy a predicate
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $L$ be a list of bit strings and $p$ a Boolean predicate on bit strings. Write $L^{+}$ for the list obtained from $L$ by replacing each string $l$ by the two strings $0 \cdot l$ and $1 \cdot l$, in this order (`L.flatMap fun l => [false :: l, true :: l]`); the enumeration of the bit strings of length $k + 1$ used by the tabulations is $(\mathrm{bitStrsOfLen}\ k)^{+}$. For a predicate $q$, $|\mathrm{filter}_q(L)|$ denotes the length of the sublist of $L$ of the elements satisfying $q$, with multiplicities.

$$ \bigl|\mathrm{filter}_{p}(L^{+})\bigr| \;=\; \bigl|\mathrm{filter}_{l \mapsto p(0 \cdot l)}(L)\bigr| + \bigl|\mathrm{filter}_{l \mapsto p(1 \cdot l)}(L)\bigr|. $$

This is the one-bit step of counting seeds by their prefix (`length_filter_take`): the class verifier of the polynomial-time halting reduction reads only the first $d$ bits of its seed of length $d + e$, so the number of seeds whose prefix satisfies a predicate is the number of prefixes that do, times $2^e$, which turns the verifier's seed count into the numerator of the compressed sampler's distribution.

**Formalization Note**. The statement is `MIPRE.Cost.Data.length_filter_flatMap_bits`, for `L : List BitStr` with `BitStr = List Bool` and `p : BitStr → Bool`; it is an equality of natural numbers between `((L.flatMap fun l => [false :: l, true :: l]).filter p).length` and `(L.filter fun l => p (false :: l)).length + (L.filter fun l => p (true :: l)).length`, with no hypotheses on `L` or `p`.

nodes.theorem_title: The body of the halting decider: a run of `body` is a run of the program `prep` selects on the input it selects
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Ambient cost model of the formalization: programs (`Prog`) run on binary-tree data (`Data`); $\mathrm{encode}$ is the size-faithful encoding of numbers, bit strings, programs and tuples as data (a tuple is a right-nested chain of $\mathtt{cons}$ cells; a datum encodes as itself); $p(v) \Downarrow_t r$ (`p.Runs v r t`) means that $p$ run on the single input $v$ halts with result $r$ at cost $t$. Fix a gap-preserving compression $G$ (`GapCompression`), an efficient universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $UT$, and a program $S'$ (the search program).

The paper-route decider of the halting verifier is built from the polynomial-time function `prep G U UT S'`: on a description $(M, (\lambda, d'))$ and an input $(n, \mathit{rest})$ it returns the pair (program to run, its input) selected by the three branches of the decider: the constant-$\mathtt{true}$ program if $M$ halts on the empty input within cost $\mathrm{size}(n)$ (the binary length of $n$), else the constant-$\mathtt{false}$ program if the search program of $(\lambda, d')$ does, else the compressed decider of $(\mathcal S^{\mathrm{compr}}_\lambda, \mathrm{wrap}\ d')$ on $\mathrm{encode}(n, \mathit{rest})$. The body `body G U UT S'` runs the program of `prep` on its input, then calls the universal machine on the pair returned.

Let $P \in \mathrm{Prog} \times (\mathbb N \times \mathrm{Prog})$, $n \in \mathbb N$ and $\mathit{rest}, r \in \mathrm{Data}$. Then

$$ \bigl(\exists t,\ \mathrm{body}(\mathrm{encode}(P,(n,\mathit{rest}))) \Downarrow_t r\bigr) \iff \bigl(\exists t,\ \pi_1(\mathrm{prep}(P,(n,\mathit{rest})))\bigl(\pi_2(\mathrm{prep}(P,(n,\mathit{rest})))\bigr) \Downarrow_t r\bigr). $$

Costs on the two sides are not related. With `dec_runs_iff`, this reduces the acceptance of the halting verifier (`accepts_iff`, blueprint `lem:dhalt-values`) to running `prep` and reading its output.

**Formalization Note**. The theorem is `MIPRE.Halting.body_runs_iff`, with $G$, $U$, $UT$ explicit. `body G U UT S'` is `.let_ (prep G U UT S').code (callVar 0 U.univ)`, with `callVar 0 q = .let_ (.var 0) q`; `prep` is a `PolyTimeFun` applied through its coercion to a function, and `.1`, `.2` project the pair it returns. $P$ is any element of $\mathrm{Prog} \times (\mathbb N \times \mathrm{Prog})$, not only a description $(M, (\lambda, \mathrm{dec}))$.

Lin, MIP^co = coRE, Proc. 58th STOC, 2026, arXiv:2510.07162 (the search branch of the decider is Lin's)

nodes.theorem_title: The halting decider satisfies its fixed-point equation: a run of `dec` is a run of `body` on its own description
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Ambient cost model as throughout: programs (`Prog`), binary-tree data (`Data`), the encoding $\mathrm{encode}$, and $p(v) \Downarrow_t r$ (`p.Runs v r t`) for a run of $p$ on the single input $v$ halting with result $r$ at cost $t$. Fix a gap-preserving compression $G$, an efficient universal machine $U$, a clocked universal machine $UT$, a search program $S'$, a machine $M$ (a program) and a parameter $\lambda \in \mathbb N$. The s-m-n map of the model is $\mathrm{hardcode}(p, d) = \mathtt{let}\ \mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{const}\,d, \mathtt{var}\,0)\ \mathtt{in}\ p$, the program that pairs the literal $d$ with its input and runs $p$ on the pair. The map $F$ = `F G U UT S' M lam` is the polynomial-time function $d' \mapsto \mathrm{hardcode}(\mathrm{body}, \mathrm{encode}(M, (\lambda, d')))$ on programs, where `body G U UT S'` is the body of the paper-route decider (`body_runs_iff`), and the decider $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{halt}}$ = `dec G U UT S' M lam` is its efficient Kleene fixed point `kleeneFix U F`: the program $\mathrm{hardcode}(K, \mathrm{encode}\,K)$ for $K$ = `kleeneProg U.univ F`, built from the program of $F$ and the universal machine.

For all data $v, r$:

$$ \bigl(\exists t,\ \mathcal D^{\mathrm{halt}}(v) \Downarrow_t r\bigr) \iff \bigl(\exists t,\ \mathrm{body}\bigl(\mathtt{cons}(\mathrm{encode}(M, (\lambda, \mathcal D^{\mathrm{halt}})),\ v)\bigr) \Downarrow_t r\bigr). $$

That is, on any input the decider has the halting behavior and the results of `body` run on the pair of its own description $(M, (\lambda, \mathcal D^{\mathrm{halt}}))$ and the input; costs are not related. This is the self-reference of blueprint `lem:halt-construction` in the form the acceptance characterization `accepts_iff` consumes.

**Formalization Note**. The theorem is `MIPRE.Halting.dec_runs_iff`, with $G$, $U$, $UT$ explicit. `dec G U UT S' M lam` unfolds to `kleeneFix U (F G U UT S' M lam)`, and `F G U UT S' M lam d` is definitionally `hardcode (body G U UT S') (encode (M, (lam, d)))`. The right-hand side uses the raw datum `.cons (encode (M, (lam, dec …))) v` rather than `encode` of a pair, because $v$ is an arbitrary datum; on a well-formed input $v = \mathrm{encode}(n, x, y, a, b)$ the two coincide. No hypothesis on $S'$, $M$ or $\lambda$ is needed.

nodes.theorem_title: Acceptance of the halting verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}$, branch by branch (blueprint `lem:dhalt-values`)
nodes.natural_language_statement:
Fix a gap-preserving compression $G$ (`GapCompression`), with compressed sampler $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{compr}}_\lambda$ = `G.sampler lam` of dimension $s_\lambda(n)$ at index $n$ and output map `G.output`; an efficient universal machine $U$; a clocked universal machine $UT$; a search program $S'$; a machine $M$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb N$. The halting verifier $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}$ = `Vhalt G U UT S' M lam` is `Verifier.ofSamplerDecider U (G.sampler lam) (dec G U UT S' M lam)`: the compressed sampler at $\lambda$ with the self-referential decider $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{halt}}$, wrapped in the question-length check. A decider accepts $(n, x, y, a, b)$ when its program halts on $\mathrm{encode}(n, x, y, a, b)$ with output $\mathrm{encode}(\mathtt{true})$; a program halts within $k$ when it has a run on the empty input $\mathtt{nil}$ of cost at most $k$; $\mathrm{size}(n)$ is the binary length of $n$; `searchP S' lam d` is the program that, on the empty input, runs $S'$ on the encoding of the description string `descOf lam d` of $(\lambda, d)$.

For every $n \in \mathbb N$ and all bit strings $x, y, a, b$:

$$ \mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}\!.\mathrm{decider}\ \text{accepts}\ (n, x, y, a, b) \iff |x| = s_\lambda(n) \wedge |y| = s_\lambda(n) \wedge \begin{cases} \mathrm{True} & \text{if } M \text{ halts within } \mathrm{size}(n), \\ \mathrm{False} & \text{else, if } \mathrm{searchP}(S', \lambda, \mathcal D^{\mathrm{halt}}) \text{ halts within } \mathrm{size}(n), \\ \mathcal V^{\mathrm{compr}}\!.\mathrm{decider}\ \text{accepts}\ (n, x, y, a, b) & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} $$

where $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{compr}}$ = `G.output ((Vhalt …).sampler.prog, (Vhalt …).decider.prog) lam` is the compressed verifier of $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{halt}}$ itself. This is the acceptance statement of blueprint `lem:dhalt-values`, from which the values at level $C$ are read off level by level.

**Formalization Note**. The theorem is `MIPRE.Halting.accepts_iff`, with $G$, $U$, $UT$ explicit. The case distinction is a nested `if … then True else if … then False else …` on the Booleans `(evalWithin M .nil (Nat.size n)).isSome` and `(evalWithin (searchP S' lam (dec G U UT S' M lam)) .nil (Nat.size n)).isSome`; `(evalWithin c v k).isSome` holds when some run of $c$ on $v$ has cost at most $k$, and `Nat.size` is Mathlib's binary length. `searchP S' lam d = hardcode (Prog.onLeft S') (encode (descOf lam d))`. No hypothesis on $S'$, $M$, $\lambda$ or $n$.
